jobs.occupation: Assistant / Associate Professor of Chemistry of "Advanced Materials Science" (m/f/d) (Professor/in - Hochschulen)
jobs.description:
Constructor University (formerly Jacobs University) is a private, state-accredited, English-language university in Bremen. We offer Bachelor, Master, and PhD programs in three schools: School of Science, School of Computer Science and Engineering, and School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences. Our principles are first-class teaching and research, international diversity, and transdisciplinary cooperation. According to the 2024 Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings, Constructor University is among the top 25 percent out of more than 1.900 universities worldwide and is ranked as the second most international university in the world. As an international university, we attract highly talented and open-minded students from all over the world. Currently, 2000 students from 120 nations live and study on our residential campus.
Constructor University invites applications from interested candidates for the following position, to be filled ideally by February 2027:
 

Assistant / Associate Professor of Chemistry in "Advanced Materials Science" (m/f/d)
(full time; 38.5 hrs./week; tenure track)

Your Responsibilities:  

The School of Science is particularly interested in candidates with a strong focus on the synthesis and physicochemical characterization of Advanced Materials. In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged. Ideal candidates combine experimental and computational approaches. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain a cutting-edge externally funded research program at the forefront of the field which complements existing research groups in the School of Science.

The successful candidate will conduct teaching in Chemistry and Advanced Materials Science (lectures and laboratory courses) at the BSc, MSc, and PhD level. They will be expected to take a pivotal role in the new MSc program “Advanced Materials” with their research experience and via the development and implementation of innovative, pedagogically sound approaches to online, hybrid and in-person teaching and learning. This will also include the advising of students on their studies, and the supervision of Bachelor, Master and PhD theses and research projects.

The university is highly supportive of junior faculty, providing both formal and informal mentoring, administrative support, as well as a flexible budget for establishing an internationally visible research group. Several opportunities exist to develop multidisciplinary research projects in collaboration with other research groups or our industrial partners and to leverage existing research facilities like a clean room, an X-ray diffractometer and a compute cluster.

Your Qualifications:  

- PhD degree in the field of Chemistry or Materials Science.
- Strong publication record in relevant international journals
- Documented research activities in the field of Advanced Materials Science
- Experience in the acquisition of Third-Party funding
- Experience in successful teaching in international and diverse environments, with an interest in applying innovative teaching and learning approaches.
- Intercultural experience and competence
- Responsible, self-motivated person able to work independently and as a part of a team
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, the language of instruction and communication on campus
- Ideally, the successful candidate should be eligible for an ERC starting grant (assistant level) or an ERC consolidator grant (associate level).

What you can expect at Constructor University: 

Constructor University consistently achieves top results in national and international university rankings.

In the CHE Ranking, the most comprehensive and detailed ranking of the German-speaking higher education landscape, Constructor University has achieved top placements every year since its first participation in 2005.

- The result counts: trust working hours for work-life balance
- Individual on-boarding, career- and development planning
- Company fitness program offers with EGYM Well Pass (former Qualitrain)
- Green campus with recreation areas, take the tour: Our Campus (http://constructor.university/student-life/campus-life/campus/virtual-tour)
- Constructor University has extensive programs on sustainability and environmental sustainability

Constructor University unequivocally guarantees the academic freedom of every member of the faculty, as well as every other member of the Constructor University community. We encourage diversity in the University in ethnic, cultural, social, religious, political, and national backgrounds, as well as in individual lifestyle. Constructor University offers full equality of opportunity to all qualified applicants and is an equal opportunity employer.
 
Your Application:   

For any further information regarding this position, please contact Prof Susanne Illenberger (Dean), via the Deans' office (DeansOffice@constructor.university).

Apply today - it's simple. We look forward to getting to know you.

Please upload your documents in a single PDF document, including a cover letter, a letter of motivation stating your field of expertise, curriculum vitae, teaching portfolio and publication record, summary of research plans and collaborations including anticipated collaborations at CU (maximum two pages), a list of essential (large) equipment needed to conduct your research, copies of certificates and diplomas, certification of English proficiency (optional), and the names and addresses of two referees in our application management system.

The deadline for submission of applications is 31.10.2026.

The position offered is tenure track, with review of performance after a first contract (assistant level) of three and a second contract after another three years. Successful evaluation leads to permanence and typically promotion to associate professor level. At the associate level, the position is immediately permanent.

The review of applications will begin immediately. Please note that only applications submitted through the official application portal will be considered for recognition.

jobs.occupation: PhD Researcher (m/f/d) AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content Generation (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
Become a part of our journey and join the Constructor Community as:

PhD Researcher (m/f/d): AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content Generation

You are expected to contribute to the development of internationally visible, foundational research in AI-driven semantic structure extraction, automated reasoning-flow modeling, and adaptive content generation. The research focuses on methods for analyzing and representing deep semantic and pedagogical structures in scientific and educational materials; high-fidelity extraction of conceptual and reasoning blocks; inference-time rationale generation; and adaptive, learner-aware sequencing of content. This includes work on semantic parsing, structured NLP, graph-based neural models, metacognitive prompting, ontology alignment across disciplines, and human-in-the-loop optimization.

In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged—particularly collaborations spanning computer science, computational linguistics, cognitive science, and the learning sciences. You will contribute to developing datasets, baseline models, personalized learning engines, reasoning-graph representations, cross-domain mapping algorithms, and RLHF-style feedback loops that improve system interpretability and instructional quality. The successful candidate will also contribute to high-quality publications, release research prototypes, and support demonstrator systems that deliver structured semantic extraction, rationale-aware content generation, and cross-domain transfer of reasoning structures.

Additionally, the successful candidate is expected to support teaching activities in areas such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, AI in Education, Knowledge Representation, and Python-based analytical seminars at the BSc, MSc, and PhD levels. Responsibilities include assisting in course delivery, advising students, supervising Bachelor/Master theses, and engaging in methodological innovation for online, hybrid, and in-person learning environments. The university provides strong support for early-career researchers, including mentorship, administrative assistance, access to computational resources, conference funding, and opportunities to collaborate with other research groups and industrial partners working at the intersection of AI and digital education.

Your Profile

- Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.
- Strong research interest and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: - semantic parsing and structured representation learning
- knowledge graphs or graph-based reasoning
- transformer models, sequence modeling, or GNNs
- natural language generation and explainability
- educational AI, personalization algorithms, or cognitive modeling
- Evidence of research potential through publications, a strong thesis, or significant projects.
- Experience or interest in innovative teaching and learning approaches.
- Ability to translate theoretical insights into engineered prototypes and systems supporting scientific or educational use cases.
- Responsible, self-motivated, and capable of working independently as well as collaboratively.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Intercultural competence and experience in international environments.
- Fluency with co-pilot tools for coding and writing.
- Fluency in English, the language of instruction and communication on campus.

Funding & Appointment Terms

The appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:

- Monthly stipend of €1,650
- Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)
- Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month
- Supplementary €550 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)

Application Details

- Expected start date: February, 2026

Application package must include:

- Curriculum Vitae (CV)
- Academic transcripts
- A detailed letter of motivation outlining research interests and career goals
- 2 recommendation letters

Applications to be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.

jobs.occupation: Research Software Engineer (all genders) HPC Code Performance Optimisation (Data Engineer)
jobs.description:
The German Climate Computing Centre (DKRZ) is the central simulation and data processing facility for the German climate and Earth system modelling community and one of the leading institutions in this field worldwide. DKRZ not only operates supercomputers of the highest performance class and one of the largest data and archive systems, but also participates in many national and international projects aimed at improving the software and infrastructure for climate modelling. Here we are offering a position as

Research Software Engineer (all genders)

HPC Code Performance Optimisation

Your tasks

DKRZ plays a significant role in a number of projects with the aim of advancing Earth System Modelling (ESM). This facilitates the advancement of scientific knowledge in the fields of Earth system modelling and climate research. In the context of the current development of digital twins of the Earth, it is necessary to adapt increasingly complex models and corresponding software to the most powerful HPC systems in Europe and ensure that those codes run stable and efficiently.

As a member of the team of Research Software Engineers (RSEs), you will collaborate with Earth System scientists to overcome technical challenges in high-performance computing (HPC) and software development. Your responsibilities will include further developing, testing and optimising existing coupled Earth System models. This will allow them to be extended with new components (e.g. ice sheet models) without compromising the efficient execution time. This is a key challenge, given the need to use resources effectively on current and future HPC systems. For this position, we are looking for candidates who are interested in the interdisciplinary implementation of Earth System models and who want to apply their programming skills to new challenges.

Qualifications / Experiences

•Academic degree in computer science, applied mathematics, computational physics/engineering or related fields with a focus on scientific computing

•Strong interest in and experience with HPC-systems and parallel programming with MPI/OpenMP

•Knowledge of programming with C/C++ and/or Fortran under UNIX/LINUX and scripting languages

•Experience in the use and programming of GPU systems for scientific applications is an advantage

•Experience in algorithms, data structures and design of scientific software is welcome

•Very good communication skills and knowledge of English

Employment conditions

We offer opportunities to work in interdisciplinary teams and have excellent connections to national and international research networks. In addition to specific implementation and support requirements from our users and project partners, your work will be characterised by the freedom to work creatively at the interface between applied computer science and the development of scientific applications. Attendance at international conferences, project meetings and hackathons facilitate further training and the presentation of your own results.

Our company is headquartered in Hamburg, but we are committed to creating a flexible working environment. We offer a remote working option, with the possibility of working from home up to 100% within Germany. Remuneration will be based on the candidate's qualifications according to TVöD-Bund. The ideal commencement date would be September 2026, although this is flexible and can be discussed on an individual basis. The position is funded by a third-party project, with a limited initial timeframe until the end of 2028.

Interested applicants are requested to compile a single pdf document containing a cover letter, a detailed CV and any additional documents (e.g. professional references). Applications must be submitted via the portalhttps://dkrz.softgarden.io/en/vacancies

Application deadline: Open until filled. Priority will be given to applications received by 23 August 2026

Questions? Dr. Hendryk Bockelmann (bockelmann@dkrz.de) will be happy to answer them in advance.

For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:

Doctoral research associate for BabylAXO detector development

Limited: 3 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FHDO021/2026 | Deadline: 02.11.2026 | Full-time/Part‑time | Remote work possible

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

The Cluster of Excellence "Quantum Universe" performs research to understand mass and gravity at the interface between quantum physics and cosmology. The research team includes leading scientists from mathematics, particle physics, astrophysics, and cosmology at the University of Hamburg and DESY. As part of the cluster's experimental program to search for hypothetical very lightweight bosons, for example motivated by dark matter and dark energy in the universe, the construction of the BabylAXO experiment will start shortly. BabylAXO will look for axions and similar particles emitted by the sun in uncharted parameter regions. The doctoral research associate will engage in the start-up phase of BabylAXO and work on the extension of its scientific portfolio.

The successful applicant will be attached to the ALPS group at DESY, which together with international partners is realizing new experimental facilities to search for new kinds of very lightweight elementary particles, works on new concepts targeting high-frequency gravitational waves and developing related technologies. Doctoral research associates will become members of the Quantum Universe Research School (QURS), which provides academic and key skills training, as well as career planning support. In addition, they will receive individual budgets to facilitate the attendance of summer schools and conferences, and to support other educational measures. Additional travel money for project-specific duties will be provided by the hosting research groups. Doctoral researchers may participate in teaching at the University and in the organization of the Cluster via an early career council.

About your role:

- Contribute to the commission and installation of the BabylAXO X-ray detection systems
- Develop a calorimeter for BabylAXO sensitive to axions from solar fusion processes and supernova explosions
- Explore synergies of the calorimeter development with medical applications

The research group „Structure and Function of Molecular Machines“ headed by Prof. Dr. Hauke Hillen at the Institute of Cellular Biochemistry is inviting applications for a 

PhD Student (f/m/d)

- Molecular & structural biology of organellar gene expression -

About us

Our group is located at the University Medical Center Göttingen (UMG) and at the Max-Planck-Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Göttingen, Germany. Our research is aimed at understanding the mechanisms of eukaryotic gene expression system, in particular those found in organelles (mitochondria and chloroplasts) or employed by viruses. To study these systems, we combine structural biology (single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, X-Ray crystallography and cryo-electron tomography) with biochemical, biophysical and cell biological approaches. For recent examples of our work, see PMID: 34489609, 34135319, 38428434, 39747487, 40050611 and 40240327.

We offer access to state-of-the art instrumentation for cryo-EM (including two 300 kV Titan Krios TEMs, a 200 kV Glacios TEM and two Aquilos 2 FIB-SEMs as well as correlative fluorescent and light microscopy devices), X-Ray crystallography and various modern biophysical techniques. Göttingen is a vibrant, international student town located in the center of Germany and, in addition to its university, is home to a number of renowned research institutes, which together form the Göttingen Research Campus.
 
Position details

The position is fixed term (3 years) and the salary will be in accordance to the German Public Sector Collective Agreement (TV-L). The position is to be filled as soon as possible. The UMG is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. We further strive for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. To apply, please submit a single PDF containing a short statement of motivation and previous experience, a CV, and the names and contacts of at least two references through the system. 

For more information, visit our lab website: http://hillenlab.uni-goettingen.de

· Combine cutting-edge structural biology, protein- and RNA biochemistry as well as cellular methods to dissect mitochondrial molecular biology from the atomic to the organellar scale
· Drive your own research project in a collaborative team with close mentoring and supervision

Postdoc in FEL Physics

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

FLASH is DESY's (and the world's first) free-electron laser user facility. Within the FLASH2020+ project, the multi-beamline FEL facility FLASH has upgraded its primary arm, FLASH1, to accommodate the first externally seeded beamline, with a 1 MHz repetition rate in burst mode. We also adapt the diagnostics on both the photon and electron beam sides to match this goal. Stability is a key factor. A stable seeded source opens the door to many new experiments. Through the ErUM-Data and LEAPS-funded proposals, we develop resource-efficient and reliable Al and machine learning methods to advance ML for photon science applications while keeping large-scale research more sustainable. We are looking for a motivated postdoc to join the team and take an essential role in advancing the capabilities of FLASH with a focus on the externally seeded FLASH1 FEL branch.

About your role:

- Investigation of the coherent properties of undulator and FEL radiation with particular emphasis on transverse and spatial coherence
- Development of machine-learning-based methods to characterize (coherent) FEL radiation and deduce electron-beam properties using non-invasive single-shot photon diagnostics
- Enhance photon diagnostic capabilities, e.g. with respect to performance on ultrashort pulses
- Integration of the developed methods into the existing FLASH diagnostic infrastructure with the aim of providing non-invasive electron-beam diagnostics and supporting beam matching and optimization
- Support of FLASH operation and participation in dedicated experiments when appropriate
- Presentation of the achieved results in scientific journals and at international conferences

About you:

- PhD or equivalent, preferably with expertise in FEL physics, accelerator physics, or related field(s)
- Strong background in physics of coherent electromagnetic radiation
- Experience with machine-learning techniques and their application to partially or fully coherent x-ray sources
- Motivation to develop diagnostic methods, concepts, or instruments for the characterization of photon pulses
- Experience with Benchmarking theory against modeled or experimental data at light-source facilities as well as experience with numerical simulations using FEL and accelerator simulation tools (e.g. GENESIS, Elegant, or equivalent) are advantageous

As part of the “Potenziale strategisch entfalten” initiative within zukunft.niedersachsen, a joint funding program of the Lower Saxony Ministry of Science and Culture and the Volkswagen Foundation, University Medical Center Göttingen (UMG) is receiving almost €20 million to further strengthen its research and innovation activities. The UMG2032 – Excellence through Focus project focuses on recruiting and establishing early-career research groups, as well as early-career postdoctoral positions. Moreover, the project supports measures to promote knowledge transfer, graduate training for medical students, the establishment of a Medical Career Center, and further specialization in securing funding from international third-party funding agencies.

The Research Management team of the UMG oversees all EU-funded and international research projects, providing comprehensive support from advising applicants and handling contract negotiations to monitoring approved projects. Additionally, we assist with applications for national grants. As part of our commitment to expanding UMG’s success in securing international funding, we are placing a particular focus on opportunities from the US and UK. To achieve this, we are creating a specialized position within our team to provide targeted support to UMG scientists, covering both the application process and project administration.

We are seeking an open-minded, native English-speaking professional to step into this exciting and impactful role.

Your Tasks

Providing independent advice and support to researchers throughout the application and management process for third-party-funded research projects, with a particular emphasis on complex international funding opportunities. This includes navigating the specific regulatory and legal frameworks of international funding bodies, thereby enhancing our capacity to secure international grants. Key responsibilities include:

- Analysis and assessment of application and funding requirements, with a focus on understanding and interpreting the intricate regulatory and legal frameworks essential for successfully securing and implementing projects funded by international bodies.
- Providing guidance and support to researchers in the preparation, design, and drafting of third-party funding applications, ensuring compliance with the specific requirements of the funding call (e.g., budgetary considerations, formalities, and alignment of project proposals with the objectives of the call).
- Conducting formal and substantive reviews of third-party funding applications to ensure compliance with both internal and external guidelines, and coordinating additional administrative processes in collaboration with relevant UMG administrative departments.
- Providing support for ongoing internationally funded projects, including tasks such as contract negotiations and preparation, amendment requests, compliance monitoring, and financial or scientific reporting. Support for ongoing internationally projects (e.g. contract preparations, amendment requests, reporting)
- Offering target-group-specific information and organizing events or workshops on international research funding opportunities and best practices.
- Contributing to the strategic development of the Research Management Office, including identifying and addressing key challenges in handling complex international funding schemes and increasing UMG's competitiveness in securing international grants.

This role requires a deep understanding of the regulatory, legal and administrative landscape of international funders, with a focus on translating these complexities into actionable guidance and strategic opportunities for our researchers. By bridging the gap between funding bodies requirements and researchers needs, you will play a key role in expanding UMG’s potential to successfully acquire and manage international research grants.

To support your success in this role, we highly encourage further professional development, including certification as a Research Administrator (e.g., through the Research Administrators Certification Council), to deepen your expertise in international grant management and funding processes.

Your qualifications

- A completed academic degree (Master’s or equivalent)
- Experience in academic management or in the administration of third-party-funded collaborative projects is an advantage
- Strong knowledge of international funding landscape, particularly in the US or UK, ideally supported by certified further training (e.g. Certified Pre-Award Administrator (CPRA®) or Research   Admin (CPA®))
- Basic understanding of interdisciplinary topics relevant to grant applications, such as research data management, open science, diversity/equality and the promotion of early-career researchers
- Effective communication skills in German, written and spoken (minimum B1 level)
- A high level of initiative, organizational skills and reliability under time pressure, combined with strong teamwork and flexibility

We offer

- Good working conditions within a dedicated and motivated team
- A varied role in an international environment
- Health and fitness supported by an excellent workplace health management program
- A comprehensive range of training and development opportunities (see also above)
- Remuneration in accordance with the collective agreement for the public sector in the federal states (TV-L), including public sector social benefits and supplementary pension provision

Application deadline is Sunday, 18th October 2026 before the end of the day. Informal inquires can be directed to Dr. Uschi Hübner (forschung@med.uni-goettingen.de), Head of Research Management.

In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number of

Postdoctoral Researcher positions.

- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -

The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. 

The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department currently hosts Ramin Golestanian (director), Philip Bittihn (group leader), Suropriya Saha (group leader), and a number of postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.

The research

The postdoctoral researchers will engage in theoretical and computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter. For more information, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).

Your profile

The ideal candidate should have:

- A PhD/DPhil degree (or comparable) with a background in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;
- Prior experience with nonequilibrium statistical physics and a strong interest in active matter physics;
- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;
- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.

The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science, covering physics, chemistry and biology.

23 Interdisciplinary doctoral PhD projects in the fields of Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials The program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid-state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray science.

Reporting to the Head of HR Business Partners, this position serves as a trusted advisor to the CSO and their global leadership team, driving initiatives that enable Evotec’s success in cutting-edge, high-performance environments.

The GHRBP works closely with senior leaders to shape and define the company’s AI and innovation strategy from a people perspective, ensuring that talent, organizational structures, and culture enable the company’s scientific and technological ambitions. Strategic Partnership & Advisory

- Lead efforts to define and address organizational capability gaps that hinder business and innovation performance.

- Foster a growth mindset culture that is inclusive, agile, and results-driven, supporting the company’s transformation into a leading innovator in the life sciences and biotech industries.

Operational Excellence

Qualifications & Experience

- Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or related field; advanced degree (e.g., MBA, MSc) preferred.

- Strong business acumen with the ability to translate strategic objectives into actionable, data-driven HR initiatives that propel growth and organizational excellence.

- Comfortable in fast-paced, highly innovative environments, with an ability to balance strategic vision and tactical execution.
- Language Proficiency: Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English and German are required.

Personal Attributes

- Strategic thinker with a strong ability to drive data-backed decisions that advance both innovation and business performance.
- High integrity, professionalism, and a commitment to confidentiality and ethical leadership.
- Proactive and results-oriented, with the ability to manage ambiguity and complexity in a rapidly changing landscape.
- A genuine interest in enabling people success and building a culture of innovation, with a deep understanding of the impact that a forward-thinking people strategy can have on technological and scientific outcomes.

Integration of quantum-based algorithms into classical computing environments, and system-levelstability/error analysis of the integrated hybrid stack.

Demonstrated experience running simulations on HPC systems

Excellent teamwork and communication skills

Fluent English (spoken and written)

Desirable

jobs.description:
Job available in 2 locations: Bremen, Kassel

Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions
Office

Job Description

A PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.

The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.

About the TRILOGY Doctoral Network

TRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.

The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.

The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.

The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.

About the PhD Project

The selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.

The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.

During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.

The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.

Key Research Activities

- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:
- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.
- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.
- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.
- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.
- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.
- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.
- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.
- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.
- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.

Candidate Profile

Applicants should have:

- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.
- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.
- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.
- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Good written and oral communication skills.
- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.
- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.
- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.

MSCA Mobility and Eligibility Requirements

As the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.

Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.

Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.

Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.

Application Documents

Applications should include:

- Cover letter
- Detailed curriculum vitae
- Academic transcripts
- Copy of the Master's thesis
- Scientific publication, if available
- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.

Selection Process

Candidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.

Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.

Key Information

Position: PhD Researcher / Doctoral Candidate

Number of positions: 1

Research areas: Physics, Engineering, Chemistry

Researcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)

Contract: Temporary, full-time

Working hours: 35 hours per week

We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.

Together with selected university partner sites, the DKFZ has established the German Cancer Consortium (DKTK) (https://dktk.dkfz.de/en) . - Lead and develop a team of Global HR Business Partners and leverage people analytics to anticipate workforce needs, risks, and business impact.

Who You Are

- Proven experience partnering with Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations leaders in complex global organizations.
- Strong track record in workforce transformation, organization design, talent management, succession planning, leadership development, and large-scale change.
- Practical understanding of GMP/GxP expectations and their implications for workforce practices, training, leadership accountability, and inspection readiness.

jobs.occupation: Global Head of Facilities Management (Fachwirt/in - Facility-Management)
jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

One of the most operationally significant roles in the new CREM structure, the Global Head of Facilities Management is responsible for leading and transforming Merck's facilities and workplace management function across a global portfolio of 340+ locations and 4.3 million m² — encompassing offices, standalone labs, warehouses and selected soft services at manufacturing sites across more than 60 countries.
This is a dual-focus role requiring transformational vision and strict operational leadership. You will consolidate our existing FM foundation into a high-performing, data-informed ecosystem designed to minimise operational vulnerability. Through uniform service delivery standards and a consolidated regional IFM vendor model, you will drive process efficiency, strengthen risk controls, and unlock strategic business value across Merck's global footprint.
The scale of the people dimension alone is significant: this role leads a global FM organisation with a substantial team within CREM, with additional headcount transferring from business sectors as the expanded remit is stood up.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- FM Strategy & Vision: Define and own the global FM strategy for CREM — establishing a unified vision, service delivery model and operating standards across all asset classes and geographies, aligned to Merck's broader corporate objectives.
- Transformation Leadership: Lead the FM transformation programme — driving vendor consolidation toward a consolidated regional IFM model, standing up site-level governance, managing the lift-and-shift of FM services from business sectors, and embedding a performance management culture across the function.
- Stakeholder Engagement: Build trusted relationships with business sector leads, site managers and senior Merck stakeholders — positioning FM as a value-creating partner and ensuring the function is responsive to business needs.
- Operational Leadership: Ensure consistent, high-quality FM service delivery and drive operational excellence across the full portfolio by standardising service delivery and optimising facilities performance — maintaining service continuity throughout the transformation and holding Regional Heads accountable for operational performance within their geographies.
- IFM Partner Management: Own Merck's most senior relationships with global and regional IFM providers — acting as the primary Merck counterpart in strategic vendor negotiations, performance reviews and vendor [AB8.1]management at a global level.
- FM Budget Responsibility: Manage the global FM budget, allocating, monitoring, and optimising operational and capital expenditure (OpEx/CapEx) across the portfolio to ensure cost-efficiency, regulatory compliance, and alignment with corporate financial objectives.
- Budget Authority: Hold direct budget authority for FM vendor contracts and operational spend across the full scope — managing significant global FM expenditure, driving cost efficiency and ensuring financial transparency across the function.
- Standards & Compliance: Establish and enforce binding global FM standards — covering vendor protocols, preventative maintenance schedules, H&S compliance, SLAs and performance penalties. Ensure consistent application across all geographies.
- Manufacturing FM: Oversee the delivery of selected soft FM services at manufacturing sites — working in close collaboration with the Quality & Compliance Lead to ensure service delivery meets the specific operational and regulatory requirements of Merck's manufacturing environments.
- Performance Management: Establish and own the FM KPI framework — tracking performance against industry benchmarks (IFMA, RICS), driving continuous improvement and ensuring data-driven decision making is embedded across the function to achieve operational excellence.
- People Management: Lead, develop and inspire a global FM organisation — including four Regional Heads and the Quality & Compliance Lead — through a period of significant organisational change, building a high-performance culture.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 15–20+ years in facilities management leadership, with significant experience managing a large, complex and geographically diverse FM portfolio within a multinational corporate environment
- Demonstrated track record of leading FM transformation — vendor consolidation, IFM implementation, service standardisation and organisational change at scale
- Direct experience managing global or regional IFM partner relationships at a senior level — contract negotiation, performance management and strategic vendor governance
- Strong financial acumen — experienced in holding direct budget authority for significant FM operational spend
- Exposure to regulated environments — life sciences, Good x Practice (GxP), pharmaceutical or chemical manufacturing — strongly preferred
- Exceptional people leader — able to lead a large, diverse and geographically dispersed organisation through transformation
- Data-driven approach to FM performance — familiar with CAFM/IWMS platforms, KPI frameworks and industry benchmarking standards
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Business Administration or a related field; IFMA CFM, RICS or equivalent professional qualification advantageous
- Fluency in English required; German advantageous given concentration of portfolio in DACH region

What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!

Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

We are the European general agency of the globally active shipping company KAWASAKI KISEN KAISHA Ltd. ("K" Line). As a leading shipping company in the RoRo business, we offer highly sophisti­cated and tailor-made mari­time trans­port solu­tions to our custo­mers from the automotive and heavy machinery indus­tries. Your responsibilities

- Support technical assessment and acceptance of cargoes incl. High & Heavy, special and project cargo as well as review of operational handling

- Openness towards digital collaboration tools such as SharePoint Lists, Planner, Loop or comparable solutions.
- Basic understanding and responsible use of modern AI models and AI-supported applications in the daily work context.

- Close collaboration with international colleagues, ports, vessels, OEMs, surveyors, and ship management teams worldwide

jobs.occupation: 573787 Business Marketing Manager IGT-Devices (all genders) (Betriebswirt/in (Hochschule) - Marketing)
jobs.description:
To support our initiatives for further adoption of Philips technology providing Class IA guideline treatment options, we are expanding our International marketing team with a Business Marketing Manager DACH, responsible for the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio.

The Business Marketing Manager is the dedicated field-based marketing owner for the DACH market zone, covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland. This role is accountable for translating international and global marketing strategy into locally relevant market activation, demand generation and adoption across the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio. The individual is expected to operate close to the market, spending significant time in the field with sales teams, customers, clinical partners and regional stakeholders to understand local needs, identify growth opportunities and remove barriers to execution.

The role combines strategic portfolio marketing with hands-on field execution. The Business Marketing Manager will define and drive DACH-specific marketing plans, shape customer engagement programs, support priority account activation, build local proof points and ensure launches, campaigns and market development initiatives are executed with strong local relevance and commercial impact.

As a member of the International Marketing team, you will own specific marketing activities that span the complete international region.

Success in this role requires regular travel and visible presence across the zone. The individual should expect to travel extensively within DACH, approximately 50-60% of time, to engage with customers, KOLs, sales teams, professional societies, congresses, workshops and other in-market activation opportunities.

Your role:

Own the DACH market zone

- Act as the primary marketing owner for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, accountable for local market planning, activation priorities and execution quality. Be present in the field with sales team, and customers to understand adoption barriers, customer needs, competetive dynamics and local growth opportunities.
- Collaborate with global and international marketing, market intelligence, and sales leadership to prioritise target accounts, market segments, and growth opportunities across the portfolio.
- Lead specific marketing capabilities internationally, strengthening the broader International marketing organization.
- Translate strategy into local execution by converting global and international portfolio strategies into DACH-specific messaging, campaigns, engagement formats and sales enablement priorities.
- Drive demand generation and adoption by leading marketing activities that increase awareness, utilization and customer preference for the full IGTD portfolio.

Partner internally, externally and represent the voice of the market

- Partner with sales leadership and field teams to prioritize accounts, shape plans, refine messaging and support commercial objectives.
- Bring structured market insights, customer feedback and competitive intelligence back to the international marketing team to influence activation planning and portfolio priorities.
- Seek and develop opportunities to strengthen Philips’ cardiology value proposition for customers in your region by close partnership with adjacent Philips categories such as the One-IGT unique solution offering.
- Build reference sites, customer testimonials, and clinical proof points that resonate with local audiences. Partner with KOLs and professional societies to strengthen Philips’ position in focus markets.
- Work under limited supervision and broad guidelines, serving as the primary marketing contact for assigned portfolio areas and focus markets.
- Define proposals for the mid-term marketing strategy, identifying key market challenges and opportunities early and implementing business plans and goals accordingly.

You're the right fit if:

- Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Healthcare, or related field.
- 3–5 years of experience in downstream marketing, preferably in healthcare, medtech, or related industries.
- Demonstrated experience managing a broad product and solutions portfolio (not limited to a single category or technology platform).
- Proven ability to lead dedicated market initiatives – owning the full marketing cycle from strategy to execution within specific geographies.
- Strong execution skills with the ability to adapt global strategies for local impact.
- Excellent presentation, communication, and stakeholder management abilities.
- Knowledge of image-guided therapy, interventional systems, or healthcare technology is a plus.
- Must be fluent in German and English languages.
- Willingness to travel 50–60% of time.

Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. The base salary range for this role is € 126,297.80 – € 159,977.21. We determine pay within the range using objective factors, like the skills the role requires, your relevant experience and the responsibility you will have in this role, alongside internal equity and local market considerations.

This role is eligible for Short Term Incentive, with your rewards linked to individual performance and company results. We will share the full approach with you during the interview process, so you can make a clear, informed decision.

Benefits include:

- Annual leave: 30 days
- Mobility and devices: subsidized Germany ticket, leasing opportunities for private use (bicycles, cars, smartphones, ...)
- Philips University & Philips in Balance: wide range of professional training courses for personal development and healthcare
- Philips Pension Fund: employer-funded pension plan
- Philips Partnerzeit: two paid weeks off after your partner has given birth
- Philips MyShop: discount on Philips products
- Culture: informal culture, a paid day for voluntary work, various team and cultural activities, etc.

How we work together
Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

About Philips
We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others.
• Learn more about our business (https://www.philips.com/a-w/about.html) .
• Discover our rich and exciting history (https://www.philips.com/a-w/about/our-history.html) .
• Learn more about our purpose (https://www.philips.com/a-w/about/environmental-social-governance/our-purpose) .
If you’re interested in this role and have many, but not all, of the experiences needed, we encourage you to apply. You may still be the right candidate for this or other opportunities at Philips. Learn more about our culture of impact with care here (https://www.careers.philips.com/global/en/our-culture) .

jobs.occupation: Scientific Coordinator (m/f/d) International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Stru (Projektkoordinator/in (kaufmännisch))
jobs.description:
The Max Planck Society is one of the world’s leading research organizations. Its institutes conduct cutting-edge basic research in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences and humanities for the benefit of society. Located in Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld, the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) investigates the properties and dynamics of matter on the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motion. Its interdisciplinary research combines experimental and theoretical approaches, with a particular focus on ultrafast phenomena, quantum materials and advanced imaging methods. The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST) is a joint initiative of the MPSD, Universität Hamburg, Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY) and European XFEL. It provides outstanding doctoral researchers from around the world with a structured and interdisciplinary training environment at the Hamburg-Bahrenfeld research campus.

To coordinate and further develop this international doctoral program, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivated

Scientific Coordinator (m/f/d) International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST)

The position offers an excellent opportunity to apply academic experience and transferable skills in a new professional context and to develop a career in science management. We are looking for a candidate who understands the opportunities and challenges of doctoral research from personal experience and is motivated to use this knowledge to support and further develop the next generation of international researchers.

Your position

- Training Programme - Develop and coordinate a semester-based curriculum of scientific courses and transferable-skills training in close collaboration with IMPRS Fellows and Principal Investigators.
- Plan and organize workshops, retreats, networking events and career-development activities tailored to the needs of doctoral researchers.
- Regularly evaluate and further develop the training program to foster interdisciplinary exchange and professional development.
- Annual International Doctoral Recruitment - Coordinate the annual international recruitment and application process, from developing and publishing doctoral projects and launching the call for applications to organizing the selection symposium, conducting interviews and coordinating final admissions.
- Doctoral Mentoring and Career Development - Support doctoral researchers throughout their time in the programme, from admission and onboarding through to completion, serving as a trusted contact for programme-related, administrative and career matters.
- Develop and coordinate initiatives that help doctoral researchers explore and prepare for career opportunities beyond the PhD.
- IMPRS-UFAST Office and Programme Administration - Oversee the day-to-day operations of the IMPRS-UFAST Office and coordinate communication, collaboration and networking among doctoral researchers, academic partners and committees, national and international partner institutions, and the MPSD administration.
- Serve as a member of the IMPRS-UFAST Executive Board and contribute to programme governance by preparing and coordinating meetings, implementing decisions, and overseeing reports, evaluations and programme documentation.
- Coordinate the programme budget and oversee the website, guidelines, application information, records and communication channels, while contributing to quality assurance, alumni relations, academic networking and the strategic development of IMPRS-UFAST.

Your background and skills

- A completed doctorate in the natural sciences; postdoctoral experience is an advantage, but not a requirement.
- A strong understanding of doctoral research, the challenges and opportunities of an academic career, and the German higher-education and research environment.
- A genuine interest in science management and in applying your academic experience and expertise in a broader professional context.
- Strong communication, coordination and project-management skills, demonstrated through experience in research, teaching, mentoring, event organisation or collaborative projects.
- A proactive, independent and structured approach to work, combined with creativity, initiative and a strong ability to work collaboratively.
- Excellent written and spoken English; very good German language skills or a willingness to develop them further are desirable.
- Intercultural sensitivity and the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with doctoral researchers, senior scientists, administrative colleagues and external partners.

- Previous experience in science management is an advantage, but not a requirement. We particularly welcome candidates with an academic background who are ready to broaden their professional perspective and bring their scientific expertise, international experience and organisational strengths into a new professional context.

Our offer

- A varied and rewarding role at the intersection of science, doctoral education, career development and science management, with scope for initiative, professional growth and the opportunity to contribute your own ideas to the further development of IMPRS-UFAST.
- An international, interdisciplinary and collegial working environment at the Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld research campus, with a modern workplace and opportunities for collaboration across institutions.
- A wide range of training and professional-development opportunities.
- A family-friendly working environment and active support in balancing work, family and personal life.
- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticket.
- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the German public pay scale (TVöD Bund), depending on qualifications and professional experience.
- Supplementary pension provision through VBL.
- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.

- The Max Planck Society is committed to gender equality, diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. The Max Planck Society also aims to increase the number of employees with disabilities and therefore expressly encourages applications from qualified individuals with disabilities.

Your application

Please submit the following documents through our online application portal by 26 October 2026.

- a letter of motivation outlining your interest in science management, doctoral training and the development of IMPRS-UFAST
- your curriculum vitae
- copies of your relevant university degrees and doctoral certificate
- relevant employment certificates or references
- a publication list, if applicable

For questions regarding the position, please contact Dr. Neda Lotfiomran (neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de) ) . Detailed information about the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter can be found at http://www.mpsd.mpg.de (http://www.mpsd.mpg.de/) .

We look forward to your application.

Job posting no. 20260820

The GWDG is seeking an

HPC Systems & Scheduling Developer (m/f/d)

to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C), full-time (39 hours per week), remunerated in accordance with TVöD E 13. The position is tied to the GWDG QC project’s runtime running till October 2029. The successful candidate is expected to contribute in developing GWDG’s QC ecosystem (see responsibilities listed below). The GWDG handles sensitive data, and in such cases, it is important that the code is human-verified for any security concerns. The applicant must demonstrate the ability to do such a verification without AI assistance in the interview.

The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers (NHR-Nord@Göttingen) in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is a partner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Furthermore, the GWDG operates HPC resources for the German Aerospace Center (DLR). As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG provides technical support to researchers and students from various scientific domains, including digital humanities, life science, earth system science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. In the field of quantum computing, the GWDG also runs the QUICS project, providing SMEs with access to quantum computing resources.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates to join the QC team at the GWDG focused on anomaly detection for industry applications. The goal is to build a platform for such use cases based on existing stacks, giving companies a tool for quantum anomaly detection.

The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, Quantum Computing, and AI.

Responsibilities

Focus: Connecting quantum workloads to GWDG’s existing HPC infrastructure. Requires a deep understanding of both classical HPC architectures and the specific characteristics of quantum jobs. The developer will take responsibility for scheduler logic, including:

- SLURM partition mapping
- Optimization of SLURM execution for Quantum Computing Jobs
- Implement HPC transpilation pipelines and, more generally, workflows for HPC/AI pre- and post-processing
- Performance tuning of hybrid workloads
- Implementation of monitoring and benchmarking mechanisms

Requirements

- PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, combined with demonstrable industry or research experience
- Ability to code in Python
- Proven coding experience (without AI assistance): scope, functions, variables, classes, array methods, etc.
- Demonstrable expertise in optimizing HPC stacks for proper system implementation and tuning
- Experience building and operating software-based services, ensuring long-term maintainability
- Knowledge in QC (quantum computing) job characteristics and resource requirements, and familiarity with compiler/transpiler pipelines
- Excellent teamwork and communication skills
- Fluent English (spoken and written)

Do you fit all the above requirements? Then we welcome your application!

Desirable

- Demonstrable experience tuning SLURM (partitioning, QoS, job prioritization policies) in a production HPC environment
- Experience benchmarking and profiling hybrid classical/quantum or GPU workloads
- Experience enabling optimal, resource-efficient operation of hybrid classical/quantum workloads
- Familiarity with monitoring and observability tooling for HPC systems (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana)
- Background in systems administration or DevOps for research computing infrastructure
- German B2 or higher

Our offer

- Flexible working hours and opportunity for partial mobile working
- A modern, diverse work environment at the intersection between academia and industry
- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center
- Qualification and further development of your skills
- Social benefits of the public sector

Your application

Have we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 30.09.2026 via our online form: https://bewerbermanagement.net/fpnhs

The GWDG strives for gender equity and diversity and therefore welcomes applications from any background. The GWDG strives to employ more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged.

If you have any questions about the advertised position, please contact Dr. Jan Cillié Louw (e-mail: jancillie.louw@gwdg.de).

- Design end‑to‑end workflows and advanced technical concepts that directly influence customer decision pathways, operational processes, and regulatory considerations

- assuming designated roles within the Safe Systems of Work, such as Authorising Engineer, Authorising Officer, or Training Mentor

- have completed a degree within electrical engineering, or equivalent
- bring strong expertise within electrical safety, including standards, laws, and regulations
- demonstrate technical leadership competence

Job Title: Metabolic Engineer (m/f/d) 

Microbial CO2 Transformation Specialist 

10 September 2026 

☀️About Us: 

Join the COLIPIan family as a Metabolic Engineer and help us develop next-generation microbial CO₂ transformation processes. 

At COLIPI, we are developing sustainable bioprocesses that use renewable carbon, including CO₂, to produce valuable microbial lipids and biomaterials. Our technology combines unconventional CO₂-utilizing microorganisms, metabolic engineering, and advanced fermentation to create sustainable alternatives to conventional lipid production. 

We are looking for an experienced scientist who can combine experimental strain engineering with metabolic modelling, systems biology, enzyme engineering, and bioinformatics to improve our production strains systematically. 

🧑🏽‍🔬Key Responsibilities: 

- Identify, design, and optimize metabolic pathways for converting CO₂ into lipids and other microbial storage molecules. 
- Develop and implement strain-engineering strategies, including gene knock-outs, overexpression, heterologous pathway expression, promoter engineering, plasmid-based engineering, and CRISPR/Cas-based approaches. 
- Establish, curate, and apply genome-scale metabolic models of our unconventional production strains to identify metabolic bottlenecks, predict engineering targets, and guide strain development. 
- Select and optimize heterologous enzymes and apply enzyme-engineering approaches to improve enzyme activity, stability, expression, and performance within the host microorganism. 
- Analyze and interpret transcriptomics, metabolomics, genomic, and sequencing data to understand cellular physiology and identify new engineering opportunities. 
- Apply bioinformatics tools for genome annotation, pathway analysis, sequence comparison, enzyme identification, and promoter/regulatory-element prediction. 
- Develop genetic tools and engineering strategies for COLIPI's unconventional CO₂-utilizing microbial strains. 
- Plan, execute, and analyze metabolic and genetic engineering experiments and translate results into iterative strain-development strategies. 
- Work closely with fermentation and analytical teams to evaluate engineered strains under relevant cultivation and gas-fermentation conditions. 

🛠️Qualifications: 

- PhD in Metabolic Engineering, Synthetic Biology, Systems Biology, Biotechnology, Biochemistry, Microbiology, or a related field, ideally combined with relevant academic and/or industry experience. 
- Strong background in microbial metabolic engineering, molecular biology, genetic engineering, and synthetic biology. 
- Hands-on experience with strain-engineering techniques such as knock-out/overexpression, cloning, heterologous gene expression, CRISPR/Cas, and directed evolution. 
- Demonstrated experience with genome-scale metabolic modelling and constraint-based metabolic analysis, ideally including model reconstruction or curation and experience with metabolic-modelling tools such as COBRApy, COBRA Toolbox, CellNetAnalyzer, etc.  
- Experience analyzing omics datasets, particularly transcriptomics and metabolomics, using computational and bioinformatics tools. 
- Good programming and data-analysis skills, ideally in Python and/or R. 
- Knowledge of enzyme engineering, protein structure-function relationships, and optimization of heterologous enzymes for activity and stability in thermophilic host microbe. 
- Strong understanding of microbial physiology, central carbon metabolism, carbon fixation pathways, metabolic regulation, and cellular redox/cofactor metabolism. 
- Familiarity with fermentation processes; experience with gas fermentation, autotrophic organisms, C1 metabolism, or non-model microorganisms is a strong advantage. 
- Experience with lipid/fatty-acid metabolism or engineering of acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA pathways is advantageous. 
- Ability to work independently, develop scientific strategies, and contribute to building and leading a highly effective strain-engineering team. 
- Legal permit to work in Europe, fluent in English (German B2 advantageous). 
- Willingness to embrace startup dynamics and help establish scalable scientific processes for future growth. 

🥰We Offer: 

- Competitive salary and 28 days of paid holidays 
- Steep learning and growth curve 
- Laptop and personal safety gear (goggles, coat, shoes) and training  
- Be part of an international team, blending academia with passionate startup vibes 
- Work on groundbreaking climate action technology with Europe's leading microbial carbon capture experts 
- Embrace an open feedback culture, flat hierarchies, and short decision-making processes 
- Access a fully equipped lab, cutting-edge technology, and ample room for personal development 
- Participation in advanced training programs 
- Annual performance appraisal meeting with manager, in addition to more frequent feedback and growth meetings

- Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the 2nd biggest city and 1st ranked city to live in Germany. 
- Experience unique maritime charm and blazing nightlife. 
- Immerse yourself in a city rich in cultural events, museums, and galleries. 

If you are passionate about leveraging biology to tackle climate challenges and want to be part of a dynamic team shaping the future, apply now to contribute to our mission at COLIPI.

You will own the end-to-end delivery of insights across one or more GSI disciplines (primary market research, competitive intelligence, or strategic forecasting), ensuring every recommendation is grounded in rigorous analysis and directly informs critical business decisions.

Working with cross-functional partners across commercial strategy, market access and pricing, other GSI functions, and regional insights teams, you will drive insights that elevate decision quality at critical stages of the asset lifecycle.

Who You Are :

- A degree in life sciences, business, economics, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience — is required.
- 5 or more years of experience in at least one global strategic insights discipline — primary market research, competitive intelligence, data analytics, or strategic forecasting — ideally within the pharmaceutical or biopharma industry.
- You have designed and led insights and KPI workstreams for in-market or launch assets, with at least 2 years of direct experience across pre-launch, launch, and post-launch phases.
- You hold deep expertise in one or more of the following: qualitative and quantitative primary market research (study design, discussion guide development, strategic recommendations); global competitive intelligence (trial monitoring, congress coverage, strategic simulation); or topline forecasting (model building, opportunity assessment, scenario analysis).
- You have global experience across two or more major markets — such as the US, China, EU4 and UK, or Japan — and bring a nuanced understanding of how market dynamics differ across regions.
- You work effectively across functions, with a solid understanding of how commercial strategy, market access and pricing, and regional insights teams each contribute to asset success.
- You are comfortable navigating the full medicine lifecycle — from proof-of-concept through in-market management — and understand how insights activities evolve at each stage.
- You communicate complex findings with clarity and confidence, translating analytical outputs into compelling narratives that resonate with senior stakeholders and drive informed decisions.
- English fluent, additional languages are a plus
