jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About the opportunity

In the position of an AI Engineer (f/m/d) you will work with our system and software teams to develop instrument control and data analysis software for laboratory devices helping our customers to get valuable insights from a biological sample. You use your expertise building real-world AI agent systems to work in an environment where AI agents support the development of medical-grade software. In this role you will set the blueprint for AI-enabled software engineering across QIAGEN, changing how our developers, testers, architects and DevOps engineers work every day.

Your tasks include

* Design and build multi-agent workflows that automate software development lifecycle processes, from planning and design through implementation, testing and documentation.
* Translate the knowledge of our teams, including architecture decisions, domain models and business rules, into reusable, machine-readable building blocks that AI agents can work with reliably.
* Build evaluation loops that measure the quality and correctness of AI-generated outputs against the standards of a regulated environment, and continuously improve them.
* Integrate AI agents with the tools our teams rely on every day, as well as to our instruments and software products using MCP servers, Git, CI/CD pipelines and REST APIs.
* Serve as lead AI engineer, guiding and mentoring junior engineers and colleagues across the development team in adopting agentic AI in their daily work.
* Collaborate with international development teams in Poland, Spain, and Denmark to strengthen and refine your technical capabilities and personal network.

 

Your profile

* A master's degree in computer science, software engineering, information systems or a related discipline
* 3+ years of professional experience in software and product development, including the successful delivery of complex software solutions in agile environments
* Strong software engineering skills, especially in Python or a comparable backend language and working knowledge of Git, CI/CD pipelines and containerization
* Experience building AI agents, agentic systems or LLM-based applications, including evaluating, testing and validating AI-generated outputs
* Hands-on experience building MCP servers or clients and integrating AI agents with other systems through APIs. Knowledge of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS) that allow AI agents to monitor and operate hardware through a common interface is a plus.
* Regular use of AI-assisted development tools in your daily work, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot
* Excellent communication skills in both English and German (C1 level)

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role) 

 

Our people are the heartbeat of everything we do. Passion drives us as we push boundaries to innovate and evolve. We inspire with our leadership and make an impact with our actions. We cultivate a collaborative, supportive environment where each individual and team can flourish. We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

What to Expect

The Bodyshop Technical Trainer position requires someone with exceptional ability to deliver learning solutions within their region. The Tesla Bodyshop Technical Trainer will take responsibility for ensuring our internal and external repair network is equipped to deliver the best ownership experience the world has ever seen for every Tesla owner. Key responsibilities include facilitating hands-on technical Onboarding and Continuous Bodyshop technical training, mentoring and supporting Bodyshop technicians, and partnering closely with local Bodyshop Managers and regional network managers to train for skill gaps and elevate the performance of their teams and regions.   This individual must be creative, proactive, organized, flexible, results-oriented, and have a passion for and understanding of electric vehicles. Must have outstanding communication, facilitation, and organizational skills while demonstrating a positive and professional demeanor.Please note that only 1 role/headscount is open, to be hired either in the UK or Germany.

What You’ll Do

- Facilitate Onboarding and Continuous instructor-led and virtual Bodyshop technical training on electric vehicles equipped with complex automotive and electromechanical systems to enable employees to perform their role safely and to Tesla’s standards

- Support local apprentice programs as needed, including delivering training, supporting apprentice mentors, and reviewing training materials

What You’ll Bring

SCHOTT Pharma designs solutions grounded in science to ensure that medications are safe and easy to use for people around the world - because human health matters. The portfolio comprises drug containment and delivery solutions for injectable drugs ranging from prefillable glass and polymer syringes, to cartridges, vials, and ampoules. Every day, a team of around 4,700 people from over 65 nations works at SCHOTT Pharma to contribute to global healthcare. The company is represented in all main pharmaceutical hubs with 17 manufacturing sites in Europe, North and South America, and Asia. Human health matters.

Tesla is seeking an Account Manager for residential energy sales in Germany. Your core responsibility is B2B sales of Tesla residential and small commercial energy products, with a primary focus on Powerwall 3P — Tesla’s three-phase home battery and integrated inverter, purpose-built for the German and European grid. Following the launch of Powerwall 3P in Germany, you will scale adoption through distributors and third-party installers, grow a high-performing partner network, and drive business development in your region. Beyond strong execution and a team-oriented mindset, successful candidates bring creativity, passion, and the drive to lead in a fast-moving technology and market landscape. * This position can be based anywhere in Germany.

- Achieve Powerwall 3P and Wall Connector sales targets within assigned channel(s) in Germany
- Build and grow relationships across partner organizations (distributors, installers, and related channels), clearly communicating Tesla’s product portfolio, three-phase value proposition, and feature roadmap

- Identify and support initiatives that improve partner training, installation quality, fulfilment, and Tesla support — with particular focus on three-phase design, commissioning, and backup use cases
- Provide user and customer feedback to IT on Tesla tools/systems and to Operations on processes

What You’ll Bring

- 5+ years in account management or channel sales within the PV or energy storage industry
- Strong understanding of residential/small commercial energy storage, ideally including three-phase (3P) systems, hybrid inverters, and grid-tied architectures common in Germany
- Working knowledge of grid/utility markets, grid connection practices, and relevant German/EU regulatory and incentive frameworks

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Project Manager (f/md) for Supplier Relationship Management & Supply Chain Resilience, you will work closely with the management team of GS D Procurement and the Gas Services Project Orion. Your role is essential to drive objectives of the ORION project to de-risk the GS D supply chain. In this role you report to the Head of Commodity Management and will work closely with the head of GS D procurement and the CPOs of the product lines, as well as the project organization in Gas Services. The tasks range from monitoring, improvement and developing the supplier relationship management and risk-mitigation in the supply chain. 

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Establish, maintain, and actively manage supplier relationship management activities
* Analyze supply chain de-risking activities across GS D, benchmark and exchange with Orion project team members on Gas Services level, drive improvements and process harmonization
* Drive cost-saving initiatives and risk-mitigation actions together with commodity managers, project management, finance, engineering, and supply chain teams
* Increase data-driven decision making, leveraging integrated supply chain tools and support of AI
* Prepare transparent project progress tracking, identifying risks and taking mitigation action with SQ, Procurement, Engineering in GS D

What You Bring

* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field, combined with project management skills, and understanding of supply chain topics across the value chain from Sales, to Engineering and to Procurement. 
* Longstanding professional experience in managing complex projects, financial analysis, procurement, or a comparable environment, typically gained over 5+ years.
* Strong collaboration, stakeholder-management, strategic-thinking, influencing, and process-improvement skills across procurement, finance, project management, and supply chain interfaces.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials from the combination of inert materials and living organism, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. Across the institute, materials scientists, synthetic biologists and biophysicists cooperate to understand living and inert matter, and to realize new materials with unprecedented functions from a synergistic interfacing.

with interest in the fundamental understanding of microbial communities within synthetic microenvironments. The candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary research team within the Department Dynamic Biomaterials at INM.

The Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

As (Senior) Manager Direct Tax Compliance & Processes, you will act as a trusted business partner to management, driving efficiency and effectiveness across tax compliance, accounting, and reporting activities. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders while contributing to tax reporting, compliance, process optimization, and strategic tax projects across the DACH region.

* Further develop and enhance the Tax Compliance Management System while proactively supporting tax governance, tax quality, and change management initiatives.
* Support annual tax reporting at both legal entity and group level, including the calculation of tax positions and preparation of tax-related disclosures under US GAAP and local GAAP requirements.

* Collaborative team player with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.

to interrogate autoimmune kidney diseases using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and bioimage analysis techniques, including deep learning

Working hours: 75% of the collectively agreed full-time working hours (currently 38.5 hours per week)

Remuneration/Rates: EG 13 (TV-L)

Project Title: Dissecting immune cell crosstalk in autoimmune kidney diseases with spatial transcriptomics and pathomics. Institute for Pathology, RWTH Aachen

Within this project the PhD candidate will interrogate immune cell crosstalk and crescent formation in patients with autoimmune kidney disease (including IgA nephropathy, ANCA-glomerulonephritis and others). The PhD candidate will learn to train and deploy histology segmentation models as part of the Aachen Digital Pathology group, as well as the downstream analysis of morphometric features in conjuncture with spatial transcriptomics.

This PhD-Program is meant to built a new generation of scientists that are rigorously trained in the development and application of cutting-edge computational tools to generate digital biomarkers with translational clinical impact. This combined skillset will enable the candidate to excel in their further academic or industry career after concluding the PhD training.

The PhD-Project is embedded within the section of Translational Nephropathology at the Institute of Pathology, offering a comprehensive training programs for PhD candidates, peer-to-peer mentoring, lectures and lab meetings on translational kidney research, as well as possibilities for networking and presentations at scientific meetings. We are an interdisciplinary and international team of scientists and clinicians with a long-standing focus and expertise in developing novel methods for digital pathology, advanced image analysis and deep learning. The German Diabetes Center (DDZ) is the Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. The DDZ is an interdisciplinary research center linking molecular and cell biological basic with clinical and epidemiological research approaches. The DDZ has the aim to develop new approaches for prevention, early detection and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and to improve therapy and treatment of its complications.
The Institute for Clinical Diabetology (Director: Prof. Dr. Michael Roden) is looking for an

Epidemiologist (postdoc - m/f/d) We are searching for a candidate with (1) a doctoral degree in epidemiology, (bio)statistics or a comparable discipline, (2) the ability to work in an interdisciplinary manner with physicians and life scientists, and (3) knowledge of epidemiological methodology and statistical analysis systems (e.g. SAS or R). Neuronal exocytosis is a highly regulated process that enables the rapid release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles. Central to this process is the controlled assembly of SNARE protein complexes, which drive membrane fusion and are regulated by a network of associated proteins. The PhD project will investigate the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying SNARE complex assembly and function in membrane-like environments. A particular focus will be placed on the development and characterization of membrane-mimetic systems, including lipid nanodiscs and synthetic copolymers, to study SNARE complexes and their regulatory proteins under increasingly native-like conditions. Cryo-electron microscopy will be combined with complementary biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterize these systems at the molecular level.
The project offers the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary structural biology environment at Forschungszentrum Jülich, with access to expertise in cryo-EM, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. Cryo-EM studies will be conducted at the state-of-the-art facilities of the Ernst Ruska-Centre (ER-C) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. The expertise in NMR spectroscopy and macromolecular crystallography at IBI-7 offers further opportunities for complementary structural and biophysical characterization. This combination of methods will enable the candidate to address biological questions from different structural perspectives and to develop a broad expertise in modern structural biology. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:

A Master’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, or a related field

Strong practical experience in protein biochemistry, including recombinant protein expression and purification
Previous hands-on experience with cryo-electron microscopy and/or cryo-EM sample preparation
Interest in membrane proteins, protein-protein interactions and structural biology
Ability to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary research team
Good communication skills in English

WE ARE HIRING

Attorney-at-Law (m/f/d)
Commercial Law (North Macedonian Law) – Full-time or Part-time (min. 30h/week)
Location: initially Dresden, Germany / prospectively North Macedonia

WHO WE ARE

At NAUTARIS. legal | tax, we are not a traditional law firm with dusty files and dictation. We are an international, digitally oriented team of over 60 lawyers, tax experts, and accountants across Germany, the Czech Republic, and Poland, delivering outstanding work. We provide holistic, practical, and forward-looking advice to businesses—both legally and tax-wise.

A particular focus of our work lies in international and cross-border matters. Looking ahead, we plan to establish our own office in North Macedonia at a central location (e.g., Skopje, Bitola, Ohrid, or similar). We see significant economic and legal potential there and aim to develop this location deliberately and responsibly, closely connected to our existing offices.

WHAT WE OFFER

- A strategically exciting position with an international perspective
- Thorough onboarding and close support during the initial phase
- An interdisciplinary and appreciative working environment
- Clear structures, short decision-making processes, and genuine trust
- The opportunity to actively help build and shape a new office location
- Long-term collaboration with development prospects
- Permanent full-time or part-time employment (min. 30h/week)
- Predictable and flexible working hours with electronic time tracking
- A modern, well-equipped workplace
- A strong team culture: shared breakfasts, team events, and celebrations that strengthen cohesion
- Further training opportunities through seminars, training sessions, and individual programs, even during the probation period
- Free beverages, massages, parking options, and attractive additional benefits such as a monthly tax-free non-cash benefit of €50

WHAT YOU BRING

- You are a fully qualified lawyer (advokat) with solid knowledge of North Macedonian law, with a focus on commercial law
- You are a well-rounded commercial lawyer, not narrowly specialized
- Ideally, you have 2–3 years of professional experience (not mandatory)
- Business-fluent German or English skills (one of the two is required), as well as openness to using translation tools in daily work
- A high willingness to travel between Germany and North Macedonia

What matters most is that you are open to new legal and economic topics and are able to familiarize yourself with international and cross-border legal matters, particularly EU law, private international law, and relevant treaties. In addition, you bring economic and organizational understanding, as well as enthusiasm for building structures and contributing entrepreneurially.

You work in a highly independent and structured manner and demonstrate integrity, discretion, and loyalty toward the firm and our clients. You communicate effectively, even across distances.

You think long-term and entrepreneurially and are able to find creative solutions to complex economic and organizational challenges.

YOUR PERSPECTIVE

- Your place of work will initially be in Dresden, Germany, for 1–2 years.
- During this time, you will gain a comprehensive understanding of our working methods, client structure, firm culture, and interdisciplinary collaboration with our tax advisory team.
- At the same time, you will be regularly involved in project-based work in North Macedonia.
- The experience and structures gained in Germany will be gradually and transformatively transferred to North Macedonia and will play a key role in establishing and supporting a new office there.
- The exact location will be determined jointly and is intentionally kept open.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

- Providing legal advice to companies in a business-oriented environment
- Advising under North Macedonian law in the field of commercial law in its full scope, in particular: - Corporate law (including company formations, restructurings, and dissolutions)
- Drafting and negotiating contracts
- Supporting location decisions and investment projects
- Employment law matters
- Interfaces with tax law in close cooperation with our tax advisors
- Advising on funding opportunities and business-related regulatory frameworks
- Supporting and actively shaping business processes
- Building, maintaining, and developing client relationships
- In the long term: co-establishing and independently managing a law firm office in North Macedonia in close coordination with the Dresden office
- Regular professional and organizational exchange with the German team

WE LOOK FORWARD TO HEARING FROM YOU

Are you interested in joining us on this journey of building a new office in North Macedonia and looking for a long-term position explicitly designed as an employment relationship? Then let’s talk.

Please send us your application documents, including your salary expectations and earliest possible start date, as a PDF to:
bewerbung@nautaris-legal.com

Ms. Sophie Kahl | sophie.kahl@nautaris-legal.com | +49 351 4383708 517
Ms. Marija Treneva | marija_treneva@yahoo.com

jobs.description:
KD Pharma Group is a medium-sized, internationally operating company headquartered in Bexbach, Saarland. We specialize in the manufacture of custom products that meet the diverse needs of the global market. KD Pharma Group is one of the few companies worldwide offering Omega-3 concentrates with a purity of up to 99.5%. This is achieved through a dedicated focus on research and technology development for Omega-3 fatty acids. This enables KD Pharma Group to provide tailored solutions, allowing each customer to differentiate themselves from competitors in the global marketplace.

We are looking for an experienced Direct Procurement Manager (m/f/d) within the Global Procurement organization, who is responsible for managing all commercial and sourcing activities related to direct materials (raw materials, packaging, and components). In this role you will drive category strategies, lead supplier negotiations, and ensure continuous material availability across sites while achieving cost, quality, and delivery objectives. This role combines a strategic partner and a hands-on executor capable of managing sourcing strategies globally while also providing direct support to sites through day-to-day purchasing activities.

Aufgaben

Strategic Procurement Leadership

- Lead sourcing, negotiation, and contracting for Direct materials to achieve savings, quality, and supply continuity.
- Own assigned categories globally develop sourcing strategies, conduct market benchmarking, and drive competitive positioning.
- Lead supplier business reviews and category meetings, ensuring alignment between Procurement, Technical, and Operations teams.
- Identify and qualify new suppliers to enhance competitiveness and reduce supply risk.
- Collaborate with Finance to quantify savings impact on P&L and ensure transparency on cost drivers.

Negotiation & Commercial Strategy

- Lead complex supplier negotiations, leveraging cost breakdowns, volume leverage, and market trends.
- Develop negotiation playbooks with the Strategic Sourcing Specialist and execute them effectively with cross-functional alignment.
- Manage long-term agreements, payment terms, and escalation clauses in line with global procurement objectives.
- Ensure compliance with group policies, contracts, and governance processes.

Analytics & Performance

- Perform independent cost and market analyses to identify opportunities for price improvement, supplier consolidation, or alternate sourcing.
- Build and maintain cost models, track raw material indices, and perform variance analysis to anticipate cost changes and negotiate proactively
- Analyze supplier quotations, freight trends, and payment-term impacts to determine the total cost of ownership (TCO).
- Transform complex data into clear insights and recommendations for category strategies and supplier negotiations.
- Collaborate with the Senior Procurement Analyst to align methodologies and validate results but maintain ownership of strategic interpretation and decision-making.
- Develop and present analytical summaries to management, highlighting risks, opportunities, and financial impact of sourcing decisions.

Supplier Relationship & Risk Management

- Maintain and improve supplier relationships through structured performance reviews, scorecards, and improvement plans.
- Ensure suppliers meet KD Pharma quality, compliance, and sustainability standards.
- Partner with QA/Technical teams to resolve non-conformances and ensure preventive actions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Lead cross-functional discussions across sites to align material specifications, MOQ rationalization, and cost-saving projects.
- Coordinate with Supply Chain and Planning to anticipate material requirements and secure capacity.
- Support key strategic initiatives such as supplier consolidation, global tenders, and payment-term harmonization.
- Support procurement excellence initiatives, SOP updates, and audits.

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Employment scope: full time / part time options are available

Type of contract: initially limited to three years;

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A later permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation. A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile

- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field
- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations
- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage
- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management
- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team
- Very good command of German (B2)
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)
- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstances

Desirable skills

- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology
- Knowledge in research data management and databases
- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum work

We offer

- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology
- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work
- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities
- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications
- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.

For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/

For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de

Contact

Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung

Senckenberganlage 25

60325 Frankfurt a.M.

For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.

E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

What to Expect

In this role you’ll support the design, construction, launch, and transfer of geartrain manufacturing lines and equipment used in Optimus Actuators. This role will prioritize successful design and launch of production line while maintaining maximum efficiency, production volume, and safety while validating performance and fully documenting all aspects of the project for handover to sustaining operations.  The ideal candidate will bring deep technical expertise in high-volume geartrain manufacturing lines and the successful introduction of new technologies to mass production line. They must demonstrate experience translating manufacturing requirements into efficient, detailed production line designs that are robust and practical to implement . In this position, you will take ownership of production line creation of specialized equipment from concept through line launch completion—defining performance requirements, running process flow simulations as needed to validate solutions grounded in first principles, and leading commissioning through final validation.

What You’ll Do

- Use CAD software and simulation tools (e.g., AutoCAD, FactoryCAD, or similar) to create 2D/3D models, floor plans, and detailed drawings that support both main production line and also supporting areas within Geartrain Manufacturing Scope
- Work with factory simulation/modeling teams to develop flow manufacturing constraints for new equipment development such as aisle sizing, incoming raw materials to the cell and work in progress areas between cells
- Install, commission, integrate and troubleshoot new equipment and tooling and support setup for manufacturing, including machines, peripheral equipment, tools, and automation systems
- Oversee the handover of commissioned lines to production teams, including operator training, documentation of procedures and manufacturing BOM, and resolution of issues during line launch
- Contribute to R&D efforts in equipment design and process development by integrating layout considerations, material flow, and facility requirements early in the innovation cycle to enable scalable and efficient manufacturing solutions
- Design and develop detailed cell and production line layouts for each gearbox, including placement of machinery and their integration to the mainline, workstations, material flow paths, utilities, and storage areas to optimize production processes and efficiency
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Factory, Infrastructure, Material Flow, Design, Manufacturing Eng., EHS personnel, and project&program leads) to integrate layouts into main factory design

jobs.occupation: Research Associate (m/f/x) Physics- and Quantum-Inspired Computing on the SpiNNaker2 (Mathematiker/in)
jobs.description:
TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.

At the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Institute of Circuits and Systems (IEE), the Chair of Highly-Parallel VLSI Systems and Neuro-Microelectronics offers a project position as

Research Associate (m/f/x)

Physics- and Quantum-Inspired Computing on the SpiNNaker2 Neuromorphic compute platform

(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting as soon as possible as part of a project funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF). The position is limited until August 31, 2028. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). 

Tasks:

In modern supercomputing, there is a trend towards alternative hardware approaches and alternative compute paradigms, as conventional CPUs are approaching scaling limits. One prominent example of such alternative approaches are quantum computers. These promise to tackle numerical problems such as monte carlo sampling or large-scale optimization, which are NP-hard for conventional CPU-based machines, through a mixture of extreme parallelism (quantum superposition) and probabilistic computing. Less prominent examples include for instance neuromorphic compute approaches such as the SpiNNaker2 system, which employs a massive amount of ARM microcontrollers (153 per chip, 5Mio in overall machine) that are embedded in a slim, low-latency communication fabric inspired from neuronal connections in the brain. It is a generally programmable computing substrate, but greatly differs from classical architectures like CPUs or GPUs, allowing for more distributed processing and simulation approaches.

Inspired by the brain, SpiNNaker2 contains accelerators for probabilistic computing, and it can utilize a large number of compute elements in an asynchronous fashion, bypassing the usual Amdahl limit of conventional supercomputers. Thus, we see SpiNNaker2 as a "quantumorphic" system, i.e. a system that, while not a quantum computer, shares certain characteristics with it. One particular focus of our group is thus on using SpiNNaker2 for physics/quantum-inspired algorithms. We have e.g. already shown better scaling than either quantum computers (in terms of scale) or conventional supercomputers (in terms of achievable parallelism) for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization. Another example could be stochastic spiking neurons for solving finite-element tessellations in a highly-parallel, asynchronous fashion, or highly parallel Monte-Carlo Sampling.

Specifically, in the project “Supercomp”, we want to apply these methods to solving real-world industrial problems in the Infineon manufacturing chain. A tentative work plan could e.g. focus around quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, where algorithms exist for classic supercomputers, quantum computers (D-wave annealers), and neuromorphic hardware.

The workplan would then be:

1. Analyze current approaches and their fit on SpiNNaker2. 
2. Choose a single algorithm or small subset for optimization and implementation. 
3. In parallel, derive with your PhD colleagues at Infineon a set of industrial benchmarks.
4. Complete a full processing chain using neuromorphic versions of QUBO or similar and 
5. hybridize/cascade/combine above approaches by networking with other PhDs of the team.

A hybrid of these approaches could potentially show advantages on SpiNNaker2 that none of the individual approaches could achieve.

Requirements: 

- university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in applied mathematics, physics, computer science or related fields of expertise
- very good programming skills (e.g. C++, Python, PyTorch)
- ability to collaborate well in an interdisciplinary environment
- fluency in technical and non-technical English
- a high degree of independence, commitment, team spirit, and good communication skills
- excellent skills and practical experience in one or more of the following research areas is beneficial: hardware/embedded Systems; probabilistic computing; quantum computing at a logical/mathematical level

We offer: 

- the opportunity for engaging and independent work within a flat hierarchy, in an open-minded team and supportive atmosphere
- flexible arrangements for work hours to support a good work-life balance
- 30 days of vacation per year (based on a 5-day workweek)
- extensive opportunities for professional development and continuing education
- health care and sports programs offered by TUD
- a discounted job ticket (also available as a Deutschlandticket)
- participation in the supplementary pension scheme for employees in the public sector via VBL (Federal and State Government Employees Retirement Fund)

TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.

TU Dresden, Chair of Highly-Parallel VLSI Systems and Neuro-Microelectronics, Prof. Christian Mayr, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.

Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.

About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. Job
Responsibilities Build Our Employer Brand Develop and implement
creative employer branding initiatives across channels such as
LinkedIn, our career website and employer review platforms. Create
compelling content, including copy, campaign concepts and ideas for
visual and video content. Bring employer branding campaigns from the
initial concept through to execution. Ensure our global employer brand
is reflected authentically in our local activities. Shape Internal
Communications Help build and develop our internal communication
channels, including digital platforms and employee newsletters.
Discover and share stories from across the organization that
strengthen our culture and foster engagement. Translate complex topics
into clear, engaging communication for employees. Support internal
events, town halls and culture initiatives that connect our growing
workforce. Collaborate Across Teams Work closely with colleagues
across HR and international stakeholders to ensure consistent and
effective communication. Act as a bridge between global corporate
communication principles and local implementation. Partner with HR and
Talent Acquisition to create a seamless employee and candidate
experience. Profile To be successful in this role, you should bring:
Professional experience in Employer Branding or Internal
Communications. Strong copywriting and storytelling skills with the
ability to create engaging content for different audiences. Excellent
communication skills in German and English (written and spoken). A
hands-on mindset with the motivation to turn ideas into action and
deliver results. The ability to work effectively with international
stakeholders in a multicultural environment. It would be a plus if you
also have: Experience building internal communication channels (e.g.
intranet, newsletters, employee communication platforms). Experience
with social media, employer branding campaigns or digital content
creation. Experience in a growing, international or greenfield
environment. Why Join ESMC? Make a Visible Impact Your ideas won’t
stay on presentation slides –they’ll become part of the culture of
one of Europe’s most exciting semiconductor projects. Build
Something New Join a true greenfield project where you’ll help shape
our employer brand and internal communications from the very
beginning. Enjoy Creative Ownership Bring your own ideas to life while
working within an international environment that values initiative,
collaboration and continuous improvement. Experience the Best of Both
Worlds Benefit from the agility and team spirit of a growing local
organization, backed by the strength and stability of global
technology leaders. Grow With Us As ESMC continues to expand, you’ll
have the opportunity to grow your role, broaden your expertise and
help shape the future of our organization Additional contact details
ESMC recruiting team will get in touch with you if your candidacy fits
with hiring criteria. Thanks!

jobs.description:

engagierte/n: Equipment Engineer (m/f/d) – Start Date: 1 October
2026 At ESMC, the Equipment Engineer supports the installation,
maintenance, troubleshooting, and optimization of advanced
semiconductor manufacturing equipment in a cleanroom environment. As
part of a high-volume 24/7 fab operation, the role focuses on ensuring
tool performance, improving uptime, reducing defects, and supporting
stable production. The position requires openness to scheduled and
occasional shift work, on call duty, includes an initial induction and
training period in Dresden of one month, followed by one year of
on-the-job training in Taiwan. If you are interested in advancing your
career in semiconductor manufacturing, learning from one of the
world’s leading semiconductor companies, and joining an
international and diverse team on a unique learning journey, apply now
with your English CV. Tasks 1. Maintain equipment performance in a
cleanroom environment to support stable, high-quality production. 2.
Handle on-duty tasks and perform fundamental alarm troubleshooting. 3.
Install and qualify new tool sets according to project plans and
schedules. 4. Identify root causes and solve critical equipment
issues. 5. Improve tool uptime and availability while driving defect
reduction. 6. Identify and pursue opportunities for hardware
capability enhancement. 7. Build defense and monitoring systems to
prevent equipment failures and performance loss. 8. Manage vendor
relationships and act as module liaison with facilities, vendors, and
manufacturing shift personnel. 9. Support scheduled night shifts,
evening shifts, weekend work, on-duty assignments, and on-call duties
as required in a 24/7 high-volume manufacturing environment. Profile

1. Legally eligible to work in Germany. 2. Available for approximately
one year of on-the-job training in Taiwan. 3. Open for scheduled and
occasional shift work, on call duty. 4. Degree in electronics,
electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mechanics,
mechatronics, material engineering, or an equivalent field. 5.
Practical experience in a mechanical or equipment-related field. 6.
Understanding of technical documentation and schematics. 7. Knowledge
of semiconductor manufacturing is a plus. 8. Fluent in English with
good command of German. 9. Hands-on working attitude with an open
mindset. 10. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. 11. Able
to perform physical work on tools in a cleanroom environment.

jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
OUR COMPANY

At Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.

The Position
Are you passionate about innovation, finding cutting-edge solutions and creating value where it matters, around the globe? At the BI global Inflammation team, we strive to deliver innovative Therapeutic and patient centric solutions by putting the patient in the center of everything we do. We foster innovative thinking as well as an agile and collaborative way of working to advance our novel programs and capabilities in Therapeutic Area Inflammation.
The Global TA Inflammation, (Senior) HEOR  Manager, brings technical expertise, driving Outcomes Research (HEOR) and Patient Related Outcomes fostering our patient centric drive. His/she will support the TA Market Access Head by providing oversight, direction, and functional support on HEOR & PRO & Access projects. He/she will be working closely with Value and Evidence Networks within our Global Business Unit and with external stakeholders.
Tasks & responsibilities

- In your new role, you develop and execute on health economics outcomes research (HEOR) & PRO strategies, demonstrating the medical and economic payer-relevant needs to optimize value of BI products.
- In this function, you generate evidence that secures optimal market access, successful HTA assessments, optimal pricing, reimbursement and formulary listing for BI products on a global scale.
- Additionally, you ensure insights to further inform development of the Target Product Profile (TPP), clinical development plan of our pipeline compounds.
- In consideration of regulatory body request and trial development, pre and post launch you will ensure relevant and new patient-reported outcome (PRO) measurement strategies to ensure that the patient perspective is captured in our clinical trial program and interact with regulatory authorities, closely collaborating with other functions.
- Besides, you ensure efficient and timely development of key HEOR deliverables (i.e. payer value stories, payer engagement tools, GVDs, economic models, retrospective database analyses, indirect comparisons, real world evidence data) for assigned BI products.
- Finally, yet importantly, you develop and maintain relevant partnerships with payers, academic research institutions, contract research organizations and other HEOR thought leaders in order to optimize the impact of HEOR & PRO research.

Additional responsibilities as Senior Manager:

- You will define long-term global development strategies for the assets, in close collaboration with the global Marketing and global Medical counterparts, to ensure optimal patient access.
- In addition, you will draft long-term publication strategies, considering the long-term global market development.

Requirements

- Graduate degree, preferably PhD in health economics, Medicine (MD), public health, pharmacy, focusing on Health Technology Assessment, PRO, Pharmacy, Medicine, Public Health
- Several years of pharma industry experience, with positions in areas of relevance for HEOR, PRO consulting or payer authorities
- Multiple years of direct experience undertaking Health Technology Assessments (HTA) & PRO including Evaluations for Regulatory and health authority interventions of pharmaceutical products
- Conducting or being part of a team working on non-interventional studies and RWE programs
- Demonstrated experience of successful regulatory, reimbursement negotiations for launching new products in key markets
- Proven track record of delivering value demonstration materials that resulted in timely patient access and adoption
- Proven ability in appraising clinical evidence (both RCTs and operational evidence)
- Profound knowledge and expertise to formulating COA strategies including validation methods, administration of measures and statistical analyses of COA data
- Excellent communication and influencing skill both in internal and external context

Additional requirements as Senior HEOR Manager:

- Long-term pharma industry experience, with positions in the areas of health economics, pricing & reimbursement, consulting, or payer authorities
- Several years of exposure to international business on a day-to-day basis
- Strong track record in value generation, demonstration and/or communication
- Highly experienced in conducting health economics/outcomes research across multiple specialty disciplines (e.g. patient reported outcomes, health economic modelling, real world data generation)

For employees with a current contract of limited duration, legal / labor agreement requirements for contract extension will be considered.
With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com﻿
Ready to contact us?
If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team,
Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or per mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.com

jobs.occupation: Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational Training (m/f/d) (Ausbildungsberater/in)
jobs.description:
About us The European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH
is a joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon, and NXP. For the
first time, TSMC, the global technology leader, is establishing a
semiconductor fabrication plant in the heart of Europe, offering
leading-edge manufacturing technologies for next-generation
semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared commitment to
strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For our future fab
in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and dedicated:
Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational Training (m/f/d)
Are you ready to strategically and pedagogically lead the end-to-end
apprentice journey for Europe's newest, most advanced semiconductor
facility? As a Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational
Training (m/f/d) at ESMC in Dresden, you will move beyond standard
administration to drive collaborative success across all core phases
of our technical vocational education. You will be the architect of
our future talent pipeline— managing employer branding at schools,
coordinating dual-training plans, mentoring Gen-Z apprentices, and
ensuring legal compliance. Fitting into our fast-paced greenfield
environment, this role offers a unique opportunity to shape the next
generation of microtechnology and industrial specialists from the
ground up! Tasks Talent Attraction & Recruitment: Design and execute
targeted school marketing strategies, represent ESMC at career fairs,
manage the applicant pipeline, conduct interviews, and issue
apprenticeship contracts. Onboarding & Pastoral Care: Serve as the
primary point of contact and dedicated mentor for future apprentices,
coordinating orientation phases and providing continuous coaching.
Training Curriculum Coordination: Design dual-training plans, manage
internal rotations across manufacturing departments, and coordinate
closely with local vocational schools (Berufsschulen).
Train-the-Trainer Support: Provide ongoing pedagogical and structured
guidance to our operational Fab trainers on the manufacturing floor.
Legal Compliance: Ensure full operational compliance with the German
Vocational Training Act (BBiG), the Youth Employment Protection Act
(JArbSchG), and other relevant educational laws. Key Stakeholder
Management: Build and maintain excellent collaborative relationships
with the local Works Council (Betriebsrat/JAV), vocational schools,
and local chambers (IHK). Graduation & Placement: Coordinate final
exam preparations, align with department managers to map out
post-graduation career pathways, and handle transition contract
processes. Profile Must-Have: Certifications: Holder of the AdA-Schein
(AEVO / Ausbildereignungsprüfung)—the mandatory qualification to
train apprentices in Germany. Education: Academic degree (B.Sc./M.Sc.)
or certified technical expert background (Staatlich geprüfter
Techniker) with a verified trainer/tester license. Experience: 5+
years of professional experience managing vocational training programs
within a technical, manufacturing, or industrial environment (e.g.,
semiconductor, automotive, automation, or chemical industries).
Regulatory & Institutional Knowledge: Strong, practical experience
working successfully with the IHK and a deep understanding of German
legal frameworks (BBiG, JArbSchG, and BetrVG). Languages: Fluent
German (C1/C2) is mandatory for official communications with
authorities, schools, and parents. Strong English skills (B2/C1) are
required for internal collaboration in our international corporate
environment. Pedagogical Drive: Exceptional communication skills with
the ability to motivate, resolve conflicts, and guide Gen-Z young
adults through their personal and professional development.
Nice-to-Have: Familiarity with cleanroom environments, semiconductor
fab safety regulations, and the technical demands of Microtechnology
(Mikrotechnologe/In). Experience setting up apprenticeship structures
in a fast-growing, ramp-up corporate environment. We offer Security &
Perspective: A permanent employment contract and career advancement
opportunities in one of Europe's leading semiconductors fabs. Company
Pension Plan & Financial Benefits: We support your financial
well-being with our robust company pension plan. As an ESMC employee,
you also benefit directly from TSMC’s performance through an
exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). Relocation Support for
Dresden: Moving for us? We’ll provide you with all the support you
will need for your relocation and your start in Dresden. Training &
Development: At the TSMC Newcomer Training Center, gain a deeper
understanding of the processes involved in operating complex
semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on training, while you
continuously expand your knowledge. Health & Well-Being: An annual
budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for sports classes,
massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit. Meals & Transportation:
Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized public
transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket). Additional contact
details Please apply with your English resume.

committed: Global Procurement Specialist / Strategic Buyer (m/f/d) Are

semiconductor Greenfield project? As a Global Procurement Specialist /
Strategic Buyer, you will take ownership of the commercial end-to-end
sourcing process for critical materials supporting our brand-new
manufacturing site in Dresden. You will negotiate high-volume global

and execute end-to-end global sourcing strategies and contracts to

laws, and ESG standards across all purchasing activities. Profile

related field. Experience: Minimum of 4 years of strategic procurement
or supply chain experience within an international industrial setting.
Negotiation Skills: Proven track record in commercial negotiations,
contract management, and strategic supplier evaluation. Languages:
Proficiency in English (C1) and German (C1) is required for seamless
collaboration with local and global stakeholders. Mindset: Strong
analytical thinking, attention to detail in contract review, and the
ability to coordinate multiple complex projects simultaneously.

training of 3-6 months at TSMC Taiwan. Nice to have: Industry
Knowledge: Prior experience in the semiconductor, chemical, or
advanced materials industry. Certifications: Professional supply chain
or procurement certifications (e.g., APICS CPIM/CSCP, ISM CPSM).
Global Mindset: Experience in collaborating with Asian business
environments; Mandarin language skills are a plus. Why Join ESMC? Help
build a completely new semiconductor manufacturing site in Europe.
Work in a highly international environment with colleagues across the

Participate in global projects and cross-functional collaboration.

Job Description

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

The Clinical Diagnostics Division (CDD) provides innovative diagnostic solutions across selected in vitro diagnostics (IVD) market segments and has been a trusted partner to the IVD industry for more than 40 years.

Our portfolio includes solutions for drugs-of-abuse testing, therapeutic drug monitoring, quality control, sepsis diagnosis, prenatal screening and more. In addition, CDD offers advanced laboratory instrumentation and high-throughput automation solutions for a wide range of clinical laboratory environments.

Our products and solutions are delivered through direct sales, regional distributors and OEM partnerships.

Territory: Eastern & Central Germany
ZIP Codes: 01, 02, 04, 06, 07, 08, 09, 30, 31, 32, 34, 36, 37, 38, 99
Field-based / Remote within the territory

Discover Impactful Work

We are looking for an experienced Account Manager (m/f/d) – Clinical Diagnostics to drive commercial growth across Eastern and Central Germany.

In this field-based role, you will take ownership of a strategically important sales territory, developing existing customer relationships while identifying and winning new business opportunities.

As a trusted advisor to clinical laboratories and healthcare customers, you will combine your scientific understanding with a consultative sales approach to identify customer needs, understand laboratory workflows and develop solutions that deliver measurable value.

You will work closely with customers, key decision-makers and internal cross-functional teams to expand our market presence, increase revenue and strengthen long-term partnerships.

A Day in the Life

- Develop and execute strategic territory and account plans to achieve or exceed annual sales targets
- Take full ownership of revenue growth, pipeline development and commercial performance within the assigned territory
- Manage, develop and grow relationships with existing key accounts
- Identify, qualify and convert new business opportunities within clinical laboratories and other relevant customer segments
- Build strong relationships with laboratory managers, clinicians, procurement teams, technical specialists and other key decision-makers
- Apply a consultative selling approach to understand customer applications, workflows, challenges and future requirements
- Position Thermo Fisher Scientific’s clinical diagnostic solutions effectively and develop compelling value propositions
- Manage the complete sales cycle, from opportunity identification and customer engagement through negotiation and closing
- Collaborate closely with Applications, Technical Service, Marketing, Customer Service and other commercial teams to deliver an outstanding customer experience
- Maintain an accurate and high-quality sales pipeline, forecast and customer data within Salesforce
- Monitor market trends, competitor activities and customer developments to identify new growth opportunities
- Represent Thermo Fisher Scientific at customer meetings, industry events, conferences and exhibitions
- Ensure high levels of customer satisfaction and develop sustainable, long-term business partnerships

Keys to Success

You combine a strong scientific or technical background with commercial drive and a genuine passion for understanding and solving customer challenges.

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Anton Khmelinskii in collaboration with Jan Padeken offers the following PhD project:
The progressive deterioration of protein homeostasis (proteostasis) is a primary hallmark of aging. As organisms age, the functionality of the proteostasis network, comprised of molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy, declines, leading to the accumulation of misfolded and aggregated proteins that compromise cellular viability. Proteostatic decline is not merely a consequence of aging but an early, causal event whereby loss of proteostasis precedes and predicts organismal decline, and its onset is sufficient to accelerate aging. Conversely, genetic or pharmacological enhancement of proteostasis network capacity can extend lifespan and suppresses age-related disease associated with protein misfolding across multiple model systems. These observations raise fundamental questions: what endogenous small molecules sustain proteostasis during aging, can their supplementation prevent neurodegenerative (and other protein folding diseases) and slow the aging process?

PhD project: Therapeutic applications of small molecule modulators of proteostasis

Organisms across all domains of life employ the accumulation of small organic osmolytes, which include molecules such as betaine and taurine, to mitigate proteotoxic stress. Recent work has also demonstrated anti-aging properties of this molecules, through yet unclear mechanisms. This project aims at dissecting the mode of action of different osmolytes using human cellular model systems and C. elegans as a model of organismal aging. We would like to address the following questions:

1. How do osmolytes affect cellular and organismal physiology?
2. Which types of stresses can be mitigated with exogenous osmolytes?
3. What types of protein misfolding pathologies (e.g., neurodegenerative diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Alzheimers's, Parkinson's, Huntington's) can be ameliorated with exogenous osmolytes?

The project is part of an ongoing collaboration between the Khmelinskii and Padeken groups, which gives you the opportunity to become an expert in a wide range of methods and experimental approaches. This includes transcriptomics, proteomics, cell and molecular biology, fluorescence microscopy and advanced high-throughput mutagenesis screening.

If you are interested in this project, please select Khmelinskii/Padeken as your group preference in the IPP application platform. Are you an ambitious scientist looking to push the boundaries of research while interacting with colleagues from multiple disciplines and cultures? Then joining the IPP is your opportunity to give your scientific career a flying start!
All you need is:

Master or equivalent
Interactive personality & good command of English
2 letters of reference

Exciting, interdisciplinary projects in a lively international environment, with English as our working language

Advanced training in scientific techniques and professional skills
Access to our state-of-the-art Core Facilities and their technical expertise

In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.8725 hours/week = 75%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Research associates (m/f/x) in scientific computing

The chair of numerical mathematics at the Ruhr University Bochum focuses on the development of efficient algorithms for solving problems in the natural and engineering sciences. A special emphasis is on hyperbolic conservation laws and high‑dimensional problems. We develop efficient numerical methods exploiting low‑rank tensor techniques and mixed‑precision algorithms. Moreover, we are interested in structure‑preserving numerical methods that are particularly adapted to the physical structure of the modeling equations, as well as in hybrid methods that couple models of different complexity for optimal efficiency. We are participating in the Collaborative Research Center on “Cosmic Interacting Matter” and are therefore especially interested in plasma‑physics applications in astrophysical environments as well as in magnetic‑confinement fusion. Recently, we have also turned to the Wetterich equation, an exact equation of the functional renormalization group, providing a systematic framework to study many‑body and field‑theoretic models such as classical and quantum phase transitions in solid‑state physics.

As a research assistant (m/f/x), you will independently develop new numerical schemes, implement and test their properties as well as analyze their numerical properties in challenging application problems. The opportunity to pursue further academic qualifications (a Ph.D.) is offered and encouraged.

jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation
- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.
- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.
- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.

Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage.
