A free night stay for you and your +1 in your first 3 months at your Zoku (dinner & breakfast) and a free night at any Zoku location for your birthday, including welcome drink & breakfast to experience Zoku as a true guest.

No boring canteen!! Staff meals enjoyed from our Living Kitchen.

• 
A personal budget unlocked after 1 year at Zoku to spend on extra days off, learning & development, extra cash or discounted vouchers. 

• 
A fun, young, and international team to grow with. Plus, exciting training and events to celebrate every step of the journey!

• 
A job at one of the 25 coolest hotels in the world, that feels like a second home and is purpose-driven.

WE LOVE PEOPLE WHO...

• 
Show their creativity through their passion for food and never settle for less.

• 
Can juggle many tasks at the same time while remaining cool headed and warm hearted.

• 
Enjoy variety in their day and are happy to switch things up, whether that means breakfast, brunch, lunch buffets, a la carte dinners or cheffing up something special for our Meetings & Events.

• 
Have experience in working independently and don't believe in traditional kitchen hierarchies.

• 
Enjoy working in an open kitchen and love to chat up a storm with our residents.

• 
Have experience in healthy homestyle cooking – vegetarian cooking skills are a plus.

• 
Have provable knowledge of various cooking techniques.

A FEW MUST HAVES

• 
You have a minimum of 1 year working experience in a kitchen or restaurant environment. 

• 
You have experience with implementing the local HACCP guidelines (Hygiejnebevis).

• 
You are fluent in English – Danish and other languages are a plus.

•

You are fully flexible, as there won't be fixed working days / hours, including availability on some weekends. Shifts include AM, Mid-shifts, and PM. 

• 
You love to work as we'll need you Full Time (37 hours- 5 shifts weekly)

• 
Available to start As Soon As Possible.

WHAT WE ARE PROUD OF 

Our fresh take on hospitality has been recognized around the world with plenty of press attention and design awards.

We’re also proudly B Corp certified at all four of our locations (Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Paris and Vienna), which means we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to social and environmental impact, transparency and accountability.

WHAT IS ZOKU

Zoku is a new type of hotel that offers a place to live, co-work and socialize in Europe's most livable cities: Amsterdam, Vienna, Copenhagen & Paris. 

Designed for the new generation of travellers, Zoku is so much more than a long stay hotel. It is a place you can call your second home, even on your first visit. Zoku is a hive of private Lofts and rooftop Social Spaces, so travellers can stay connected and well rested as they live and work throughout Europe. Throw yourself into your work and play, and effortlessly discover one of our home cities.

The Role

Your responsibilities will span five main areas:

·       Operations & Execution — approximately 30%

·       New Business Development — approximately 20%

jobs.occupation: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
jobs.description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (copy of original and an official English translation).  

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is 31 December, 2026, at 11:59 PM / 23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process. 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is 1 March 2026 (may be adjusted by mutual agreement) or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Senior Support Specialist, Telecom, Location: Danmark - Esbjerg
jobs.description:
Are you technically curious, service-minded, and motivated by helping customers resolve critical technical issues? Do you enjoy combining troubleshooting with coordination and clear communication? If so, this could be your next career opportunity. 

Your position 

As our new Senior Support Specialist, Telecom, you will support the daily operation of our customers communication Systems. You will take ownership of incoming requests, gather the necessary technical information, assess urgency and operational impact, and perform structured troubleshooting. When specialist assistance is required, you will coordinate the correct escalation and ensure that customers remain informed throughout the process.

You are not expected to be the specialist for every system. Your role is to establish a clear overview, perform the agreed initial checks, document findings and decisions, and ensure that each case is resolved.

Your place of work will be at our Global HQ located in Esbjerg in a full-time position. You must be willing and able to participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation according to an agreed schedule.

Your tasks & responsibilities

jobs.occupation: Laboratory technician at DTU Metabolomics Core - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
The DTU Metabolomics Core at DTU Bioengineering, Kgs. Lyngby, is looking for a skilled and motivated Laboratory Technician to join our team of excellent scientists and technicians collaborating on microbial molecules, trying to unravel their importance in nature, and discover how they can benefit humanity in various ways, such as in agriculture, and novel pharmaceuticals.

About the DTU Metabolomics Core
The DTU Metabolomics Core in the Department of Bioengineering is one of a several Core facilities within the Department that supports a wide range of research and teaching. The area in which the Metabolomics Core specializes is in the chemical analysis of small secondary metabolites from microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and microalgae. This analysis is undertaken in our extensive instrument suite (HPLC, LCMS, GCMS, MALDI etc.), a collection of instrumentation that you will work closely with as our new technician.

The primary job areas of responsibility
As Laboratory Technician in the Metabolomics Core, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of the facility in close collaboration with the Facility Manager. Your responsibilities will include:

• Operating and maintaining our analytical instrumentation, including high-resolution LC-MS systems (sample preparation, calibration, QC runs, routine troubleshooting and preventive maintenance in cooperation with service engineers)
• Running samples for internal researchers and external contract projects, from sample preparation to data acquisition
• Ordering and managing laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemicals, and keeping the lab stocked and organized
• Maintaining lab standards: cleanliness, safety, waste handling, documentation, and quality control routines
• Supporting users of the facility with practical guidance on sample submission and preparation
• Contributing to the ongoing development of workflows and procedures in the facility
• Supporting students
In addition to this is it expected that you will take part in some Department duties, particularly involving laboratory and chemical safety. This will be done in close collaboration with a team of 4 other technicians working within the same section that hosts the Metabolomics Core.

Qualifications
We expect that you:

• Hold a degree as a laboratory technician (laborant) and/or a BSc/MSc in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field
• Have hands-on experience with HPLC instrumentation. Experience with high-resolution MS (e.g., QTOF) is a strong advantage
• Are experienced in routine laboratory work, including sample preparation, solvent handling, and general upkeep of analytical labs
• Have knowledge of Good Laboratory Practice, safety regulations, and documentation standards
• Are structured, detail-oriented, and able to plan your own work independently
• Enjoy collaborating with researchers of different backgrounds and communicating in English (our working language)
• Ideally, have experience with natural products chemistry, and sample preparation
What we offer in return
With this job we offer you an exciting and versatile position in a multicultural, respectful and dynamic research and learning environment with many international employees and students. You will gain hands on experience with a wide variety of different analytical instrumentation and have the freedom to create your own daily agenda by prioritizing your tasks.

You will have:

• A central role in a well-equipped core facility with diverse and exciting projects spanning microbiology, natural products, and industrial collaborations
• Close collaboration with leading research groups at DTU Bioengineering
• A flexible, informal working environment at DTU's Lyngby campus
• Professional development opportunities, including training on new instrumentation and methods
Salary and appointment terms
Salary and appointment terms are in accordance with the OAO-S Joint Agreement and the organization agreement for Office Clerks, Laboratory Technicians and IT staff (HK/stat). In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for clerical employees OR laboratory technicians: https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The appointment is permanent full time. The position starts 1st December 2026 or as soon as possible after.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 4 November 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Facility Manager, Aaron Andersen by e-mail (ajca@dtu.dk) or by telephone (+45 45 25 61 38). DTU Bioengineering website: https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/english.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Department of Biotechnology and Biomedicine (DTU Bioengineering) is an international leader in the areas of biotechnology and biomedicine. Our engineering approach to all aspects of biotechnology and biomedicine positions us as a valuable player with unique competences in a growing bio-based economy and with health systems transforming towards personalized medicine. We have a clear focus on the needs in life science- and biotech industries and point towards innovation, new businesses, and scientific services for the benefit of society. The department has extensive collaborations with national and international research units and industry. DTU Bioengineering has approx. 400 employees, of which 2/3 are scientific staff. The department is located at DTU Lyngby Campus.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Software Engineering: Program Analysis and Repository Mining
jobs.description:
A 2-year postdoctoral researcher position is available at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) in the Software Engineering section of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI). The successful candidate will contribute to the VILLUM Experiment project “Is Correctness Necessary? An Experiment in Test-Free Program Repair.” The project investigates whether software bugs can be repaired using information found in the code itself, without relying on test suites or specifications. The position is available from February 1, 2027. 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Project Description

Generating code is becoming cheap; establishing whether it is correct is not. Large language models can now produce and modify software at remarkable speed, and practices such as “vibe coding” are widening the gap between code generation and validation. Requiring a carefully designed test suite or specification for every generated fragment is unlikely to scale. Yet most automated repair techniques depend on exactly such a correctness oracle: without a failing test or specification, they have neither a clear repair target nor a way to assess a proposed change.

This project challenges that dependency by investigating whether software bugs can be repaired using evidence already present in the code. It will combine program analysis with patterns mined from existing software to explore whether multiple, independent sources of evidence can guide repair when tests or specifications are unavailable. The approach will be studied across different programming languages and evaluated on both real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants. The broader aim is to determine when code contains enough information to support its own repair and when knowledge of the intended behavior remains essential.

 

What we offer 

We offer a dynamic and supportive research environment within an internationally recognized institute. You will join an open, collaborative team that values teamwork, professional diligence, and innovation. The Software Engineering section provides flexible work conditions and strong support for individual development, including mentorship and opportunities to expand your skills and responsibilities.

As part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, our section is involved in a variety of national and European research projects and enjoys a robust network of academic and industrial partners. This position provides an opportunity to engage with these collaborations and work on real-world challenges. We encourage and support our postdocs to publish their research in renowned journals and conferences, and to engage in knowledge exchange with colleagues and external research and industrial partners. The working language is English, and we pride ourselves on a diverse, inclusive, and inspiring workplace that fosters personal and professional growth.

 

What we expect 

The appointed researcher will investigate whether software defects can be repaired without relying on test suites or specifications. The candidate will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of a framework that combines program analysis with patterns mined from existing software. The work will involve experiments with real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants across multiple programming languages. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who meets the following qualifications and characteristics:

• 
A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Programming Languages, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field.

• 
Research experience or a strong interest in one or more of the following areas: program analysis, mining software repositories, automated software engineering, software testing, or software repair.

• 
An interest in software reliability challenges arising from AI-generated and AI-modified code.

• 
Experience with empirical evaluation, software repositories, or bug benchmarks is an advantage.

• 
Experience with one or more of C, Java, and Python is an advantage.

• 
Proficiency in written and spoken English, with good communication skills.

• 
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a research team.

• 
A strong research record or demonstrated research potential through publications or other relevant research outputs.

 

Workplace description 

The postdoc will be employed in the Software Engineering section at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), SDU. MMMI is an internationally recognized research institute within the Faculty of Engineering, known for its contributions to software engineering, robotics, and artificial intelligence. The Software Engineering section encompasses a range of research areas in software development, data analytics, and intelligent systems, and it plays a key role in several ongoing European projects.

Our workplace is truly international and collaborative. Researchers in the section come from diverse backgrounds and work closely together on cross-disciplinary projects. We benefit from state-of-the-art facilities and a strong administrative and technical support structure. The institute maintains close collaboration with other departments and centers at SDU, as well as with industry partners, providing a vibrant environment where theoretical research meets practical application. The position will be located on SDU’s Odense campus, which offers an attractive setting and a rich campus life in the city of Odense, Denmark’s hub for robotics and technology development.

 

Further information 

For further information, please contact Associate Professor Abhishek Tiwari (abti@mmmi.sdu.dk) or Assistant Professor Jyoti Prakash (jyp@mmmi.sdu.dk)

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from February 1, 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

You will be given responsibility for strategically important customers, all of which are market-leading OEMs or system providers, including those in the truck sector. Your role will be to expand and enhance the sales turnover among existing customers, while at the same time cultivating new customer relationships. A significant part of the role also involves making sustained efforts to secure up-to-date framework agreements and contracts in addition to communicating customer requirements and expectations.

The sales process consists of offering to produce the customers’ cast iron components. Once the items are being produced, the sales work will involve continuously negotiating and adjusting the sales prices of the individual components, as well as negotiating and maintaining other commercial conditions. Your normal working day will vary from administrative tasks at the office in Holstebro, where you will work closely with Production, the Production Engineering Department (PED), Business Controlling and other company stakeholders. As part of a cross-organisational partnership, you will familiarise yourself with the customers’ projects and thus become the most important link of the contact between the customer and your colleagues across the entire organisation.

When out visiting customers with a view to sales, you will always have a ‘One Stop Shop’ cast iron solution to call upon. By this, we mean that BIRN is able to cast, machine, assemble and surface-treat the products so that they can be delivered directly to the customer’s production line or application without further processing. Are you looking to combine your technical curiosity and skills with a strategic responsibility for sales and long-term customer relationships in an international industrial group? If so, you may be the person we are looking for as a Key Account Manager.

·       Searching for, analysing and developing new customer potentials and market segments

·       Close internal collaboration with production engineering, quality, controlling and finance

·       Participation in sales and strategy activities across the organisation

The position involves some travel, primarily in Europe.

·       Extensive advanced technical training/experience, ideally supplemented with commercial skills, e.g. engineer, marine engineer or equivalent. A skilled trade background, supplemented by commercial training or experience, is another option

·       Experience of technical sales, project sales or Key Account Management; alternatively, you will have been recently trained and have the right level of drive. The start date will be adapted to suit the right candidate

·       A strong professional environment with close collaboration across the Group

·       Good opportunities for both professional and personal development

·       Attractive terms and conditions of employment, including a pension scheme and health insurance

·       A good canteen scheme and active staff association

·       An informal work environment that focuses on well-being, responsibility and sustainability

ABOUT THE BIRN GROUP

Vald. BIRN A/S in Holstebro is the Group Headquarters of one of Northern Europe’s largest foundry Groups. jobs.description:
Are you an experienced leader with a strong track record in offshore wind operations, service delivery, or project execution? Do you thrive in dynamic environments where safety, customer focus, and operational excellence go hand in hand? Then we look forward to your application as Area Manager (f/m/d) for Main Component Exchanges!

Your position
In your new position as Area Manager (f/m/d) for the Main Component Exchanges, you will lead the regional delivery of our offshore MCE business across Northern & Central Europe or the UK. You will be accountable for regional performance and play a key role in ensuring the successful execution of complex offshore campaigns.

The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel regularly depending on your main place of work. The projects are typically short- and long-term service contracts for our clients in Northern and Central Europe as well as the UK.

Your tasks & responsibilities
As Area Manager (f/m/d), you will be responsible for the overall performance of your region and ensure that customer commitments are delivered safely, efficiently, and predictably. You will provide leadership across Project Management, Operational Management, and Marine Operations while maintaining strong relationships with customers and key stakeholders. The role combines strategic oversight with operational leadership and serves as the primary escalation point within the region.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to:

• Leading regional project and operational delivery performance
• Ensuring successful delivery of customer commitments regarding safety, quality, schedule, and cost
• Prioritizing resources and resolving cross-project conflicts
• Managing customer, operational, and project escalations
• Supporting strategic workload and capability planning
• Driving collaboration across Project Management, Operational Management, and Marine Operations
• Ensuring implementation of the MCE operating model across the region
• Supporting Sales & Business Development through customer, market and operational expertise

Your profile & qualifications
We are looking for an experienced and communicative Area Manager (f/m/d) who is passionate about Main Component Exchanges within Offshore Wind and wants to take ownership. You have a proactive and organised approach to your work.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management, or a related discipline
• Proven leadership experience in offshore wind, marine operations, energy services, or a comparable industry
• Strong understanding of project delivery, operations, and customer management
• Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders
• Excellent communication and decision-making skills
• A strong HSEQ mindset and commitment to safe execution
• Fluency in English, both written and spoken

Welcome to Semco Maritime
At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is motivated by solving real technical challenges, improving operational and equipment reliability, and helping scale a first-of-a-kind process toward commercial production.

Do you have solid experience from an industrial or manufacturing environment, and do you thrive in a setting where not everything has been fully built or established yet? Then we would very much like to hear from you.

 Read more about the role in the below job description.

Job description

The position:

As Mechanical engineer, you will play a hands-on role in establishing, stabilizing, and improving the mechanical performance of our first-of-a-kind tile production facility in Ikast. This role will work closely together with Operations, Maintenance, Quality, and Process Engineering to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient plant performance. You will help translate innovative process science into robust day-to-day manufacturing at the first of a kind facility, while driving structured problem-solving, equipment reliability, ppm, plant expansion support, and continuous improvement across the facility.

You will support the scaling of this process to our first commercial facility from engineering design and equipment selection through commissioning, start-up, and operations working together with our project department and our EPC firms.

Responsibilities also include:

• 
Mechanical Operations & Equipment Reliability

• 
Provide day-to-day supervisory and execution support for electrical and mechanical systems and production equipment across the tile manufacturing process.

• 
Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis for mechanical failures, downtime events, and recurring equipment issues.

• 
Help establish preventive and predictive maintenance routines for critical equipment, utilities, and production assets.

• 
Support commissioning, start-up, and scale-up activities in a FOAK environment, helping to translate development work into reliable plant operation.

• 
Production Support & Continuous Improvement

• 
Partner with Operations and Quality teams to improve equipment performance, uptime, process stability, and product consistency.

• 
Contribute to waste reduction, line efficiency, and standardization efforts as production scales.

• 
  Technical leadership

• 
Support the development of SOPs, technical work instructions, equipment care standards, and troubleshooting guides.

• 
Coordinate with vendors, contractors, and internal teams on equipment modifications, installation work, and performance improvements.

• 
Project engineering and commercial facility scale-up

• 
With the Director of projects and an EPC firm, act as Biomason’s lead mechanical engineer supporting the development of FEL3 and detailed engineering design packages including participation in and review of Block Flow Diagrams (BFDs), Heat and Material Balances (HMBs), Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), General Arrangements (GAs), Basis of Design (BoD) documents, equipment specification and selection, and HAZOP (Hazard an Operations study).

• 
Support the commissioning and startup of the commercial facility through:

• 
Participation in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) at vendor sites as needed and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) at the facility.

• 
Provide on-site technical leadership during the "boots-on-the-ground" commissioning phase, troubleshooting mechanical, thermal, or other deviations in real-time.

• 
Bridge the gap between EPC firms and internal operations to ensure a seamless handover.

What we are looking for:

• 
Experience

• 
Minimum 5 years of experience in mechanical engineering, maintenance engineering, or a similar industrial role.

• 
Strong experience in industrial process or manufacturing environments, ideally with automated or semi-automated production equipment. Concrete manufacturing or other heavy industry is bonus but not essential.

• 
Experience with motors, heat exchangers, airflow and hydraulics is a strong advantage.

• 
Basic electrical experience testing logout tag out.

Experience supporting production start-ups, greenfield projects, FOAK environments, or first-time industrial implementation is strongly preferred.

Technical Expertise

Experience working with crane and conveyance systems is a critical requirement of this position

• 
Strong understanding of industrial mechanical systems, equipment reliability, maintenance strategies, and structured troubleshooting.

• 
Experience with 5S, good manufacturing practices, and continuous improvement in a production setting.

• 
Ability to read technical drawings, manuals, equipment layouts, P&IDs, and supplier documentation.

• 
Familiarity with Six Sigma, Lean manufacturing principles, root cause analysis methodologies, and continuous improvement practices is an advantage.

Management & Interpersonal Skills

• 
High attention to detail, with the ability to manage complex, detail-oriented projects and ensure disciplined follow-up through execution.

• 
Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work across functions and cultures, preferable experience from a matrix organization..

• 
Structured, practical, and data-informed approach to problem-solving and decision-making.

Contractor control

Fluency in English is essential

On a personal level, the role needs the following approach:

• 
Proactive with a practical approach and the ability to be hands-on

he laboratory team performs tasks including:

Assessment of oocytes

Administrative duties, including tasks related to the export of tissues and cells

We have an excellent working environment and work very well together across professional disciplines. We respect and make use of each other's expertise while keeping up with developments in the field and continuously improving our overall professional standards.

We also have a strong social community. We eat lunch together every day, enjoy spending time together and occasionally meet outside working hours. We value our positive working environment highly and make a genuine effort to protect it. It is therefore important to us that our new colleague feels at home and fits well within the team.

You are a qualified embryologist.

Sufficient time to carry out your daily duties and a high degree of influence

Opportunities for professional and personal development

Friendly and positive colleagues

An organisation with a short path from decision to action

About Memtrace

AI coding agents are fast, but they forget. They lose context between sessions, repeat mistakes, and don't understand the codebase around them. Memtrace builds the memory layer that fixes this: a deterministic knowledge graph of your code, built with AST parsing rather than guesswork, that any coding agent can use. Our products include MemDB, MemFleet, Cortex, and a code review engine. We are backed by Antler and Innovation Fund Denmark, and we work with Google, AWS, and Microsoft for Startups.

The role

You will own revenue end to end: strategy, pipeline, pricing, partnerships, and the first commercial team. We have developer interest and active pilots with enterprise customers. Your job is to turn that into repeatable, paying adoption. At this stage you will do the selling yourself while building the playbook that others will follow.

Convert pilots into contracts, with clear success criteria, pricing, and procurement paths.

• 
Set pricing and packaging for individual, team, and enterprise tiers.

• 
Build channel and ecosystem partnerships (cloud marketplaces, consultancies, industry bodies, AI-coding-tool vendors).

•

• 
Hire and lead the first commercial team (sales, solutions, customer success) when the time is right.

•

What we are looking for

• 
8+ years in B2B software sales or commercial leadership, with at least one role in developer tools, data/AI infrastructure, or open-source-led products.

• 
A track record of closing enterprise deals yourself, ideally in the Nordics or wider Europe.

• 
Experience selling to both technical champions and executive buyers, and knowing how those conversations differ.

• 
Comfort with ambiguity: you have built a sales motion without an existing playbook, brand, or team.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc positions within Robotics for Laboratory Automation
jobs.description:
SDU Robotics is currently extending the team within the project CAPeX which focuses on robotics for laboratory automation. We therefore invite applications for one or more fully funded postdoc positions. The position is for a 2-year period with a starting date January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The workplace is at SDU's main campus in Odense, Denmark, and the work is expected to be primarily onsite.

 

What we offer

• 
An exciting opportunity to work at the cutting edge of robotics for real-world applications.

• 
A collaborative and supportive work environment that encourages innovation and creativity.

• 
Opportunities for professional growth and leadership.

• 
Access to state-of-the-art technology and resources.

• 
An opportunity to collaborate with excellent researchers within the Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery

 

Job description

SDU Robotics currently has an open 2-year postdoc position in relation to CAPeX; specifically, for the development of a robotic solution for automation of laboratory experiments that require manipulation of tubes, fragile glass vials, and liquids. The robotic solution should be flexible in the sense that it should be able to conduct several experiments with little user-intervention, operate alongside humans, and recover from failures. Consequently, visual feedback must be used for adapting robot behavior to a dynamic environment.  The postdoc should contribute to the deployment of the developed solution in laboratories in both SDU and DTU. The successful candidate will work closely with other PhDs and postdoc candidates in CAPeX.

As a postdoctoral researcher, your role will encompass mainly research, but teaching responsibilities could also be part of the employment. The main duties and responsibilities include: 

• 
Research in collaboration with colleagues from SDU Robotics and CAPeX.

• 
Conducting scientific research and publishing the results in high quality scientific conferences/journals.

• 
Supporting the team in securing external funding.

• 
Contributing to the project CAPeX deliverables. 

 

Profile and requirements

The position requires research experience at PhD level in a relevant area such as robotics, preferably applied to robotic systems controlled using visual feedback. The candidate is hence expected to have most of the following qualifications:

• 
Expert knowledge in the control of robots

• 
Experience in simulation of robotic systems

• 
Experience in design and development of robotic systems

• 
Experience with using computer vision.

Furthermore, the successful candidate is expected to:

• 
Have excellent knowledge of English (written and spoken).

• 
Be able to work well and communicate expert knowledge in an interdisciplinary team.

• 
Have the ability of working independently.

• 
Have a strong sense of responsibility.

• 
Conduct independent research. 

 

Research environment

The candidate will be integrated into the SDU Robotics unit, which is a team of approx. 60 employees. We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team with flexible work organization and support for individual development.

SDU Robotics is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and located at the main Campus in Odense, at the core of the Odense Robotics Cluster involving 120+ startups and established companies in robotics. The group is involved in a variety of national and European projects and features a strong network of academic and industrial partners.

We are a team specialized in robot solutions involving modelling, estimation, and control of advanced robot systems. In addition, the candidate will be integrated into CAPeX - a pioneer center for accelerating P2X materials discovery and working on automation of laboratory experiments.

CAPeX is a 13-year and 300 MDKK “Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery”, funded by Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, the Danish National Research Foundation, the Carlsberg Foundation, the Lundbeck Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and the Villum Foundation. CAPeX is hosted by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and co-hosted by Aalborg University (AAU), and unites leading experts from DTU, AAU, University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, and the University of Southern Denmark with international partners from Stanford University, Utrecht University, and the University of Toronto to form a truly Pioneering Center on P2X. You can read more about the CAPeX research themes and X-trails, our organization, and the other open PhD and postdoc cohort positions at http://www.capex-p2x.com. 

We look forward to receiving your application and to supporting your academic growth as a researcher in SDU Robotics. 

 

Further information 

Further information about this position is available via email from Professor Christoffer Sloth chsl@mmmi.sdu.dk.

Please visit us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/sdu-robotics. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

The application deadline is October 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Employment as a postdoc requires scientific qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
A motivation letter that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages).

• 
Detailed Curriculum Vitae, including personal contact information. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications.

The application may also include: 

• 
Research statement. 

• 
Summary of experience in teaching. 

• 
References (names and emails) and/or reference letters.

• 
Documentation of other qualifications with relevance for the position. 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from January 1, 2026. Extension may be possible depending on available funding (no more than 4 years at the same university).

The workplace is at SDU's main campus in Odense, Denmark, and the work is expected to be primarily onsite.

Research will be predominant in the position. Teaching assignments can be agreed individually. Furthermore, other types of assignments may occur to a limited degree. The faculty determines the distribution of the various assignments. The weighting of the different assignments may vary over time.

Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

A relatively large part of our research is fertilised and inspired from clinical challenges, identified in the hospital, in our ambulatory field practice or from our external collaborators. Based on these, we want to set a new standard for cross-disciplinary research, education and innovation within animal health and disease.

  The Section for Medicine, Surgery and Reproduction for Large animals holds research and clinical teaching, in a modern 24-hour open university veterinary teaching hospital and ambulatory field practice service for all large animals with horses as the primary species consulted. We also have the cross departmental, University of Copenhagen Centre for Veterinary Simulation, which is open 24/7 for veterinary students to practice clinical skills. Our research is focused on diseases of clinical relevance for horses and cattle thereby having a direct application for veterinarians and animal owners. Also, translational research bridging basic science to companion animal as well as human medicine is a strength of the section.

  We have a strong educational and scientific focus on the athletic horse collaborating with internationally recognised research groups within cardiovascular, airway and orthopaedic research with a high impact translational research profile. To fully exploit the scientific and clinical potentials, the muscular development and disease understanding in sports and rehabilitation medicine both in horses and companion animals and is a strategic research area in the department, why collaboration with the companion animal sections of the department is expected in the position. The announced associate professorship is crucial to enhancing and strengthening this area to fully obtain the synergy of the other research areas mentioned above.

  Equine medicine is a core discipline in the fourth and fifth years of the veterinary medical education in Denmark. Therefore the position is highly involved in research based teaching of veterinary students within equine sports medicine  and the candidate is expected to take a leadership role in conducting clinical relevant research, teaching and examining undergraduate students, as well as assist and promote the development of both pre-and postgraduate teaching as well as research strategies within the field of equine sports medicine.  

  The culture of the department is typical Scandinavian: a flat structure with a tradition for close collaboration where all employees are expecting openness, mutual respect, and sharing of ideas, resources and competences.

  Job description

  In considering applications for the associate professorship, the main emphasis will be on the following aspects:

   	
• The applicant's ability to document a high level of original scientific production at an international level within the area of equine sports medicine and preferably with a strong translational profile. 	
• The applicant’s practical experience within equine general medicine in both a hospital and in research setting. 	
• The applicants experience with development of clinical research-based teaching of veterinary students.   The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• Research-based pre-and postgraduate teaching, including clinical teaching and service, associated examination and course responsibilities 	
• Strengthen, developing and integrating muscular research in research-based teaching of veterinary students 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers and veterinary students as well as securing external funding. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate and engagement in topics of relevance for horse owners 	
• Organizational contribution to the section, department and university incl. e.g. participation in department committees and course leadership. 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership.

  Find information about each criterion.

  The successful applicant should:

   	
• Hold a DVM with license to practice in Denmark or be willing to apply for such within 6 months. 	
• Hold a PhD degree or similar qualifications. 	
• Diplomat degree within ECEIM, ACVIM or ECVSMR is an advantage. 	
• Document a high degree of research experience and scientific publications within the field of equine internal medicine and sports medicine at an international level, including considerable contributions to the development of the academic discipline. 	
• Have experience with research management and other management functions, including attraction of external funding and group leadership. 	
• Document pre-and postgraduate clinical teaching experience within the field of the position and documented pedagogical training at university level. 	
• Perform research-based teaching. 	
• Perform quality patient care and service management in an equine hospital and ambulatory field practice within equine general medicine. 	
• Possess good interpersonal and communicative skills. 	
• If Danish is not the first language, the applicant is expected to obtain sufficient Danish skills within 1-2 years.   Diversity and International Applicants

  The University of Copenhagen is committed to fostering diversity and encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background.

  Useful resources:

   	
• www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility) 	
• www.workingconditions.ku.dk.   Terms of employment

  The position is a permanent position.

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Employment is as associate professor according to the collective agreement or job structure under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  This position comes with an opportunity to negotiate a start package for up to 2,500,000 DKK that will help leverage the candidate’s scientific deliverables in the initial years of employment. The negotiation for the start package takes place as part of the recruitment process. Please read about the contents of the programme and conditions, as well as UCPH’s extensive support for international researchers here

  Questions

  For further information, please contact group leader Tina Holberg Pihl thpi@sund.ku.dk.

  Application

  The application must be submitted in English, by clicking on "Apply online" below, and must include the following:

   	
• Application, including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• Diplomas - (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• Upload a list of maximum 5 publications to be assessed 	
• Research plan (3-5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines)   The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's job portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments.

  The closing date for applications is 29 October 2026 23.59 p.m. CET.

  Employer: Department of Veterinary Clinical and Animal Sciences, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Homepage: http://ikvh.ku.dk/english/

  The University of Copenhagen actively influences current and future generations through excellent research, education and co-operation. UCPH is one of the highest ranked universities in Europe and is Denmark´s oldest university, founded in 1479. Today, the University has 37,000 students and

  9,000 employees affiliated across six faculties: humanities, law, natural sciences, social sciences, health sciences and theology www.ku.dk/english.

jobs.occupation: Workshop Mechanic - Gadbjerg, near Vejle, Denmark
jobs.description:
About us

We run a workshop about 15 km from Vejle in East Jutland, Denmark, in close partnership between GMT and Nordic Rebar ApS. You will be employed by Nordic Rebar ApS, which is based at the workshop.
GMT trades in used machinery for the rebar industry and is a well-known player in the industry across most of the world.
Together, we hold a large stock of used machines that continuously need to be inspected and refurbished, and we are therefore looking for a mechanic who will make the workshop his or her permanent base.

About the job

As a workshop mechanic, you will be responsible for keeping the workshop running and the machines in good order. Your tasks will include:

·         Repair and preparation of used machines for the rebar industry
·         Loading and unloading machines and accessories using a forklift truck (a valid forklift/truck licence is required)
·         General maintenance and tidiness in the workshop

The workshop has an office attached to it, so you will have good colleagues around you, and we have lunch together.

The workshop has modern facilities, including a laser cleaner for removing rust and dirt, and we place great emphasis on the work being carried out safely and properly.

In the workshop itself you will typically be the only mechanic on a daily basis, so you must be able to plan and carry out your tasks independently.
 
We expect you to

·         Have a technical/trade background, e.g. as a car or truck mechanic, industrial electrician, or mechatronics technician, with good mechanical aptitude
·         Have at least 10 years of relevant work experience
·         Hold a valid forklift/truck licence
·         Be responsible and have a can-do attitude
·         Be able to work independently and organise your own working day
·         Not be afraid of getting dirty
·         Understand and speak English

Please note:
You must be an EU/EEA citizen. Applicants who do not meet this requirement should not apply.

Terms of employment

This is a permanent position with Nordic Rebar ApS, on the terms and under the rules and legislation applicable in Denmark.
·         Starting salary: EUR 25 per hour, paid monthly
·         Weekly working hours: 37 hours - overtime may occur and can possibly be compensated with time off, among other things to allow for more frequent trips home, if needed
·         Start date: as soon as possible
·         Workplace: Gadbjerg, approx. 15 km from Vejle
·         Accommodation (a smaller apartment/room) can be arranged locally - expected rent approx. DKK 4,000-5,000 per month max
 
Application

Applications should be sent by e-mail to ud@gmtaps.com.

Questions are welcome and can be directed to Ulrich Deichmann, GMT, tel. +45 20 98 94 44, or Arne Hansen, Nordic Rebar ApS, tel. +45 51 46 20 50.

Job description:
Want to build C++ software that helps power the next generation of autonomous and unmanned systems?At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our technology brings together computer vision, C++ software, autonomy, embedded systems and real-world product development.

We are looking for a C++ Software Engineer to join our engineering team and contribute to the software that connects and powers different parts of Robotto's technology platform.This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys building reliable systems, solving complex technical problems and seeing their software move beyond development into real-world operation.

The role:
You will develop and maintain C++ software across Robotto's software ecosystem, working on applications and services that support the operation, communication and coordination of our unmanned systems.Depending on the project, your work may span different parts of our platform-from software running alongside our autonomous systems to applications used to configure, control and interact with them.You will work closely with engineers across computer vision, autonomy, embedded software, electronics and testing to develop new capabilities, integrate components and continuously improve the reliability and performance of our systems.

What you will do:
- Design, develop and maintain high-quality software primarily in C++.
- Build software used across our drone and unmanned-systems platform.
- Develop reliable communication and data flows between different software and hardware components.
- Work on performance-sensitive and potentially real-time or near-real-time applications.
- Integrate software with APIs, networking components, sensors and wider system infrastructure.
- Debug complex issues across interconnected software systems and identify root causes.
- Contribute to software architecture and technical design decisions.
- Write maintainable, testable and well-structured production code.
- Participate in code reviews, testing, documentation and continuous improvement of our engineering practices.
- Collaborate closely with computer vision, embedded, autonomy and hardware engineers.
- Support integration and testing on real systems and drone platforms.

What success could look like in your first 3-6 months:
- You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto's software architecture and how the different parts of our platform work together.
- You are contributing production-quality C++ code to our products.
- You have taken ownership of features or components from development through integration and testing.
- You are successfully debugging and solving issues across interconnected systems.
- You are contributing to improved reliability, maintainability and performance of our software.
- You have become a trusted technical partner within the engineering team.

What we are looking forWe are looking for a strong software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems and building software that interacts with real systems.
- Strong professional experience developing production-quality software in C++, with a solid understanding of modern software engineering practices.
- Solid understanding of software architecture, data structures, algorithms and object-oriented design.
- Experience developing multi-component or distributed software systems.
- Experience with networking, inter-process communication, APIs or communication protocols is highly relevant.
- Good understanding of concurrency, multithreading and performance considerations in C++.
- Experience with debugging, testing, version control and modern software development practices.
- Experience with Linux-based development environments is an advantage.
- Experience with robotics, drones, autonomous systems, defence technology or other complex technical products is an advantage, but not a requirement.
- Experience working with software that interfaces with hardware or real-world systems is an advantage.
- Professional fluency in English.
- A degree in computer science, software engineering, robotics or a related field is preferred; equivalent practical experience is equally welcome.

Please apply even if you don't meet every single point. We are interested in what you can bring to the team, your ability to learn and your motivation to work on the challenges we are solving.

Who you are:
Beyond your technical or professional experience, we care about how you work and collaborate.You:
- Are curious and enjoy solving complex problems.
- Take ownership and follow things through.
- Communicate openly about progress, challenges and risks.
- Are comfortable in a growing company where priorities can evolve.
- Enjoy collaborating with people across different disciplines.
- Value testing, learning and continuous improvement.
- Want to contribute rather than simply execute a predefined set of tasks.

Why join Robotto?
Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision, autonomy and real-world operations.You will be joining Robotto at an exciting stage of our journey as we continue to grow our team, technology and products.

Our teams work across software, computer vision, control, electronics, hardware and real-world testing. This means you will work closely with people from different technical disciplines and see how your work contributes to the wider product.

We are an ambitious and collaborative team, and we value people who take ownership, challenge ideas constructively and want to help build both great technology and a great company.This is not a role where everything is already defined. You will have the opportunity to:
- Work on challenging technology with real-world applications.
- Have meaningful ownership and influence over your area.
- Work closely with talented colleagues across multiple disciplines.
- See your work move from an idea or prototype into real-world use.
- Help shape how we work as the company continues to grow.

More information and application:
 https://careers.robotto.ai/jobs/8397119-software-engineer-c

Do you want to build computer-vision technology that helps autonomous drones understand and navigate the real world?

At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our work brings together computer vision, edge computing, software, electronics and real-world product development.We are looking for a Senior Computer Vision & AI Engineer to take a leading technical role in developing and improving the perception capabilities behind our drone platform.You will work on challenging real-world problems where robust vision, accurate localisation and reliable performance matter. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys going beyond algorithms and prototypes to build computer-vision solutions that perform reliably in demanding real-world environments.

The role:
You will join a highly technical engineering team working on autonomy for drones and unmanned systems.You will take significant ownership of computer-vision capabilities supporting object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry and other perception-related challenges.You will work closely with software, control, flight-test and electronics colleagues to turn computer-vision concepts into robust, deployable solutions.As a senior engineer, you will also contribute to architecture and technical decisions, help strengthen engineering practices and share your experience with other engineers across the team.

What you will do:
- Design, develop, test and improve advanced computer-vision algorithms for Robotto's drone and autonomy platform.
- Take technical ownership of computer-vision problems from exploration and prototyping through implementation, evaluation and deployment.
- Work with object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry, visual SLAM and related perception challenges.
- Build robust solutions that can perform under changing environmental and operational conditions.

- Contribute to code quality, testing, documentation and engineering practices.
- Share knowledge and provide technical guidance to other engineers where relevant.

What success could look like in your first 3-6 months:
- You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto's autonomy platform, architecture and computer-vision priorities.
- You have taken ownership of one or more important perception challenges and are driving them towards robust solutions.
- You have contributed meaningful improvements to areas such as object detection, tracking, localisation or visual-inertial odometry.
- Your solutions are being evaluated against real-world data and operational scenarios.
- You are contributing to architecture and technical decisions across the computer-vision stack.
- You are collaborating effectively across computer vision, software, control and flight testing.
- You have become a trusted senior technical contributor within the engineering team.

What we are looking for:
We are looking for an experienced engineer with a strong computer-vision foundation and a track record of turning complex technical ideas into practical, working systems.
- 5+ years of relevant professional experience preferred, with significant hands-on expertise in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, autonomy or a closely related field.
- Strong practical knowledge of computer vision, with experience in areas such as object detection, tracking, visual localisation, visual-inertial odometry, visual SLAM or related perception methods.
- Strong C++ programming skills, with Python experience for algorithm development, experimentation, testing and prototyping.
- Experience taking computer-vision or machine-learning solutions beyond research and prototyping into real products or deployed systems.
- Experience designing, training and evaluating deep-learning models for computer-vision applications.
- Experience deploying and optimising models or computer-vision algorithms on edge or resource-constrained computing platforms is highly relevant.
- Strong understanding of algorithm evaluation, datasets, testing methodologies and measurable performance criteria.
- Experience contributing to architecture or technical-design decisions within complex software or perception systems.
- A good understanding of how vision systems interact with cameras, sensors, software, compute platforms and real-world environments.
- Experience with drones, robotics, autonomous systems or embedded-adjacent software is a strong advantage.
- Experience mentoring, supporting or sharing technical knowledge with other engineers is an advantage.
- Professional fluency in English.
- A degree in computer vision, robotics, computer science, engineering or a related technical field is preferred; equivalent industry or research experience is equally welcome.

Who you are:
You are technically curious, analytical and comfortable taking ownership when the answer is not immediately obvious.You enjoy going deep into difficult technical problems, while keeping sight of the goal: building technology that works reliably in the real world.
- You take ownership of technical problems and drive them towards practical solutions.
- You are comfortable making technical decisions and explaining the trade-offs behind them.
- You challenge assumptions constructively and are willing to explore new approaches.
- You care about robustness, testing and measurable performance.
- You collaborate naturally across computer vision, software, control, electronics and flight testing.
- You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping others solve difficult technical problems.
- You are comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as the company and technology develop.
